ArchitectureConfig.description: Features, layers and the modules around them.

shared.description: Modules every feature may import; they must not import features.
shared.title: Shared

composition_root.description: Modules that wire everything; nothing may import them.
composition_root.title: Composition Root

wiring.description: Provider modules (whole-segment * allowed) that may import across layers and features; they keep their feature and layer.
wiring.title: Wiring

layers.description: The layers and what each may import.
layers.title: Layers

import_graph.description: Which imports count in the architecture graph.

members.description: Root-only uv workspace boundaries: source member path glob -> {may_depend_on: [target member globs]}. Unmatched source members are unrestricted; '.' names the root project. ARC009 checks direct imports.
members.title: Members

packages.description: Public interfaces and required modules for matching packages.
packages.title: Packages

canonical_exports.description: Definition or alias to its canonical public export.
canonical_exports.title: Canonical Exports

ArchitectureConfig.title: ArchitectureConfig

default.description: Whether features may import each other at all.

allow.description: Allowed imports: "layer -> layer" for all features, or {from: feature.layer, to: feature.layer}.
allow.title: Allow

base.description: Fully qualified project exception that production code raises instead of builtin exceptions (MOD008), e.g. app.errors.AppError. Omitted: {} lifts an outer policy.
base.title: Base

allow.description: Builtin exception names that may still be raised, in addition to NotImplementedError, StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, GeneratorExit, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, e.g. [TypeError].
allow.title: Allow

root.description: Package whose direct child packages are the features.
root.title: Root

FileNamingConfig.description: Canonical spellings for project configuration filenames.

yaml_extension.description: Canonical YAML extension, without a dot (LAY007). Omitted means either spelling is allowed. Applies below the project root, including hidden configuration directories, subject to project.exclude.
yaml_extension.title: Yaml Extension

compose_basename.description: Canonical Compose basename (LAY007), including dotted variants such as compose.override.yaml. The extension is controlled only by yaml_extension. Omitted means either basename is allowed.
compose_basename.title: Compose Basename

FileNamingConfig.title: FileNamingConfig

rule.description: Rule name, family, code prefix or ALL to ignore within the specified scope.
rule.title: Rule

style.description: relative: prefer relative first-party imports up to max_relative_level, absolute beyond it; absolute: always use absolute imports.
style.title: Style

max_relative_level.description: Maximum dots in a relative import when style is relative. Cross-root and deeper imports stay absolute.
max_relative_level.title: Max Relative Level

ImportsConfig.description: Which imports the dependency rules look at.

transitive.description: Also check indirect layer, feature, shared, composition-root and third-party dependencies through all reachable project modules. Reports a shortest import chain; external packages are leaves.
transitive.title: Transitive

type_checking_cycles.description: include follows the global type_checking setting; ignore excludes TYPE_CHECKING edges from cycle graphs only, retaining their configured treatment in other boundary checks. The modules scope checks concrete modules; existing scopes aggregate architecture nodes.
type_checking_cycles.title: Type Checking Cycles

ImportsConfig.title: ImportsConfig

path.description: Dotted layer path relative to a feature or root package.
path.title: Path

modules.description: Qualified module names or package prefixes outside the feature grid assigned to this layer.
modules.title: Modules

third_party.description: Which third-party packages the layer may import (ARC003).

MemberBoundaryConfig.description: Allowed target members for each matching source member.

may_depend_on.description: Workspace-relative member globs this member may import; [] forbids imports of other members. Overlapping source entries combine their allowances.
may_depend_on.title: May Depend On

architecture/layer-boundary.title: ARC001: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
architecture/layer-boundary.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.
architecture/layer-boundary.markdownDescription:
**ARC001 — architecture/layer-boundary**

A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.

Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import SqlVoiceSessionRepository
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.ports import VoiceSessionRepository

# gateway/bootstrap.py wires SqlVoiceSessionRepository to the port
```

Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain architecture/layer-boundary` for details.

architecture/cross-feature-import.title: ARC002: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
architecture/cross-feature-import.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.
architecture/cross-feature-import.markdownDescription:
**ARC002 — architecture/cross-feature-import**

A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.

Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/infra/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import CallLog
```

**Preferred**
```python
# billing/application/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.api import CallSummaryQuery
```

Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

Run `smelt explain architecture/cross-feature-import` for details.

architecture/forbidden-third-party-impor.title: ARC003: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.
architecture/forbidden-third-party-impor.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.
architecture/forbidden-third-party-impor.markdownDescription:
**ARC003 — architecture/forbidden-third-party-import**

A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.

Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
```

Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.

Run `smelt explain architecture/forbidden-third-party-import` for details.

architecture/import-cycle.title: ARC004: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.
architecture/import-cycle.description: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (ARC001, ARC002, ARC006) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.
architecture/import-cycle.markdownDescription:
**ARC004 — architecture/import-cycle**

Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.

Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (ARC001, ARC002, ARC006) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/application/invoices.py
from gateway.features.voice.application import calls
# voice/application/calls.py
from gateway.features.billing.application import invoices
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/calls.py publishes an event;
# billing/application/invoices.py subscribes to it.
```

Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

Run `smelt explain architecture/import-cycle` for details.

architecture/shared-imports-feature.title: ARC005: A shared or central module imports a feature module.
architecture/shared-imports-feature.description: A shared or central module imports a feature module. Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.
architecture/shared-imports-feature.markdownDescription:
**ARC005 — architecture/shared-imports-feature**

A shared or central module imports a feature module.

Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
from gateway.features.billing.domain import Currency
```

**Preferred**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
class Currency: ...
```

Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.

Run `smelt explain architecture/shared-imports-feature` for details.

architecture/composition-root-leak.title: ARC006: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.
architecture/composition-root-leak.description: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module. Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.
architecture/composition-root-leak.markdownDescription:
**ARC006 — architecture/composition-root-leak**

A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.

Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.main import container
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
class StartSession:
    def __init__(self, sessions: VoiceSessionRepository) -> None: ...
```

Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain architecture/composition-root-leak` for details.

architecture/non-public-module-import.title: ARC007: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.
architecture/non-public-module-import.description: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module. Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Discovered tests, including conftest.py and tests inside the contracted package's configured test roots, are outside callers and must use the public API. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. Layer and feature policies apply independently. Repair: Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.
architecture/non-public-module-import.markdownDescription:
**ARC007 — architecture/non-public-module-import**

Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.

Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Discovered tests, including conftest.py and tests inside the contracted package's configured test roots, are outside callers and must use the public API. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. Layer and feature policies apply independently.

**Problem**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.storage import OrderStore
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.api import place_order
```

Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.

Run `smelt explain architecture/non-public-module-import` for details.

architecture/missing-facade-export.title: ARC008: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.
architecture/missing-facade-export.description: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export. A contract's min_importers_to_export threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional architecture.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before. Repair: Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. Dynamic imports, implicit package initialization and import order are not proven. No exports, imports or policy are rewritten automatically.
architecture/missing-facade-export.markdownDescription:
**ARC008 — architecture/missing-facade-export**

A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.

A contract's min_importers_to_export threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional architecture.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before.

**Problem**
```python
# app/browser/__init__.py is empty
# Three outside modules each use:
from app.browser.base import BrowserEvents
```

**Preferred**
```python
# After reviewing ownership and initialization behavior:
# app/browser/__init__.py
from .base import BrowserEvents
__all__ = ['BrowserEvents']
# callers
from app.browser import BrowserEvents
```

Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. Dynamic imports, implicit package initialization and import order are not proven. No exports, imports or policy are rewritten automatically.

Run `smelt explain architecture/missing-facade-export` for details.

architecture/member-boundary.title: ARC009: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist.
architecture/member-boundary.description: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist. Member-local layers describe internal design; workspace member boundaries describe which projects may depend on one another. Only direct production imports between discovered members count. Unmatched source members are unrestricted, overlapping source globs combine their allowances, and imports inside one member always pass. Wiring and shared modules retain these boundaries. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply. Repair: Move the dependency to an allowed member or invert it behind an interface; change the root allowlist only if the dependency belongs in the intended design.
architecture/member-boundary.markdownDescription:
**ARC009 — architecture/member-boundary**

A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist.

Member-local layers describe internal design; workspace member boundaries describe which projects may depend on one another. Only direct production imports between discovered members count. Unmatched source members are unrestricted, overlapping source globs combine their allowances, and imports inside one member always pass. Wiring and shared modules retain these boundaries. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply.

**Problem**
```python
# packages/core/src/core/model.py
from api.http import serve
# root policy: architecture.members: {'packages/*': {may_depend_on: []}}
```

**Preferred**
```python
# services/api/src/api/http.py
from core.model import Order
# root policy: architecture.members: {'services/*': {may_depend_on: ['packages/*']}}
```

Move the dependency to an allowed member or invert it behind an interface; change the root allowlist only if the dependency belongs in the intended design.

Run `smelt explain architecture/member-boundary` for details.

architecture/undeclared-member-dependenc.title: ARC010: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency.
architecture/undeclared-member-dependenc.description: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency. One shared import graph makes undeclared imports work locally, but the member may fail when installed independently. This rule compares direct production imports with project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and tool.uv.sources. Distribution names are normalized independently of Python package names. Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations. Repair: For an allowed dependency, declare the imported member's distribution in project.dependencies and configure its uv workspace source. If architecture.members forbids the dependency, remove the import or move the dependency behind an allowed member boundary.
architecture/undeclared-member-dependenc.markdownDescription:
**ARC010 — architecture/undeclared-member-dependency**

A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency.

One shared import graph makes undeclared imports work locally, but the member may fail when installed independently. This rule compares direct production imports with project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and tool.uv.sources. Distribution names are normalized independently of Python package names. Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations.

**Problem**
```toml
[project]
name = "api"
dependencies = []
# api imports core.model
```

**Preferred**
```toml
[project]
name = "api"
dependencies = ["core-lib"]
[tool.uv.sources]
core-lib = {workspace = true}
```

For an allowed dependency, declare the imported member's distribution in project.dependencies and configure its uv workspace source. If architecture.members forbids the dependency, remove the import or move the dependency behind an allowed member boundary.

Run `smelt explain architecture/undeclared-member-dependency` for details.

architecture/unknown-layer.title: ARC011: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.
architecture/unknown-layer.description: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers. Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer. Repair: Move the code into a declared layer, or assign its package to the intended layer. Use the layer's modules list for packages outside features.
architecture/unknown-layer.markdownDescription:
**ARC011 — architecture/unknown-layer**

A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.

Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer.

**Problem**
```python
voice/
  domain/
  application/
  models/      # not a layer
  helpers.py   # in no layer
```

**Preferred**
```python
voice/
  domain/
    models.py
  application/
```

Move the code into a declared layer, or assign its package to the intended layer. Use the layer's modules list for packages outside features.

Run `smelt explain architecture/unknown-layer` for details.

architecture/unclassified-module.title: ARC012: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.
architecture/unclassified-module.description: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root. Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package can be assigned to a layer's modules list. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped. Repair: Add the package to the intended layer's modules list, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.
architecture/unclassified-module.markdownDescription:
**ARC012 — architecture/unclassified-module**

A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.

Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package can be assigned to a layer's modules list. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped.

**Problem**
```python
gateway/
  platform/db.py    # neither shared, a layer nor a feature
```

**Preferred**
```python
# smelt.yml
architecture:
  modules:
    gateway.platform: infrastructure
```

Add the package to the intended layer's modules list, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.

Run `smelt explain architecture/unclassified-module` for details.

architecture/uncovered-source.title: ARC013: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.
architecture/uncovered-source.description: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason. A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer. Repair: Select missing production packages and assign their architecture role. Move unclassified implementation into an existing layer. Deliberately excluded code needs project.exclude entries with path and reason. Coverage gaps cannot be hidden by debt, inline ignores or a narrowed check.
architecture/uncovered-source.markdownDescription:
**ARC013 — architecture/uncovered-source**

Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.

A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer.

**Problem**
```yaml
# smelt.yml
project:
  root_packages: [backend]
rules:
  architecture/uncovered-source: error
# A new workspace library exists but is not selected or classified.
```

**Preferred**
```yaml
# smelt.yml
project:
  root_packages: [backend, client]
  source_roots: [backend/src, libs/client/src]
rules:
  architecture/uncovered-source: error
architecture:
  layers:
    infrastructure: {modules: [client]}
```

Select missing production packages and assign their architecture role. Move unclassified implementation into an existing layer. Deliberately excluded code needs project.exclude entries with path and reason. Coverage gaps cannot be hidden by debt, inline ignores or a narrowed check.

Run `smelt explain architecture/uncovered-source` for details.

Repair: Implement the missing module in the matching package. If that package should follow a different structure, narrow or split the contract. complexity/excess-attribute-depth.title: CPX001: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes.
complexity/excess-attribute-depth.description: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes. An instance method that reaches through several stored collaborators depends on their internal arrangement. This opt-in Law of Demeter review reports calls with at least two consecutive attribute accesses from the instance receiver before the first method call, such as self.browser.input.motor(). One finding covers a whole receiver call chain. Direct collaborator calls, pure data reads and fluent chains starting from a direct collaborator are excluded. Module objects stored from unshadowed imports or declared as ModuleType, explicit SimpleNamespace trees, and typed dataclass/Pydantic record paths ending in known containers or values are namespaces rather than collaborator graphs. Known pathlib parent paths and subprocess pipes also retain their standard APIs. Namespace evidence comes from annotations, direct constructor assignments and property return annotations; analyzed imports and re-exports are followed without executing code. Every intermediate object must be a known namespace or value: a record containing a service does not exempt navigation into that service. Names such as api, client, get or append alone exempt nothing. Unknown SDK types and dynamic property/data flow remain review limitations. Decorated and implicit class/static methods, nested helper bodies, comprehensions, receiver rebinding and navigation through parameters, aliases or subscripts are outside the review. This is a bounded review, not proof of a design defect. When namespace evidence is incomplete, the finding includes the declared/constructed root type and the unresolved step. These are review inputs for an agent, not proof that the API is poorly designed. Inspect the public API contract before choosing a refactor; an intentional namespace can be a valid conclusion. Repair: Review whether the caller should receive the needed collaborator directly or ask its direct collaborator to perform the operation. A local variable alone does not reduce structural coupling. Preserve factory/property evaluation and object lifetimes; repeated lookups need not return the same object. Keep intentional API navigation with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned CPX001 suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable with rules: {complexity/excess-attribute-depth: hint}, globally or in a package override, or --select CPX001.

complexity/inline-call-argument.title: CPX002: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.
complexity/inline-call-argument.description: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument. Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded. Repair: Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.
complexity/inline-call-argument.markdownDescription:
**CPX002 — complexity/inline-call-argument**

An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.

Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded.

**Problem**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    return Response(
        text=await browser.clipboard.read(),
        users=[to_user(user) for user in result.users],
        active=sum(user.active for user in result.users),
    )
```

**Preferred**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    text = await browser.clipboard.read()
    users = [to_user(user) for user in result.users]
    active = sum(user.active for user in result.users)
    return Response(text=text, users=users, active=active)
```

Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain complexity/inline-call-argument` for details.

complexity/excess-positional-parameters.title: CPX003: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows.
complexity/excess-positional-parameters.description: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows. Call sites such as connect(user, run, tab, True) do not say which value is which, and swapping two arguments of the same type still type-checks. The max of the rule entry is the limit (5 when omitted); parameters after that limit must be keyword-only so every call names them. self and cls are not counted, nor are *args and **kwargs. Dunder methods, @overload and @override definitions are exempt because their signatures are dictated elsewhere, and tests are not checked. Positional-only parameters count like any other positional parameter. Repair: Insert * after the last allowed positional parameter, then pass the remaining arguments by keyword at every call site. Callbacks whose positional signature is fixed by a framework keep it with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {complexity/excess-positional-parameters: {severity: warning, max: 3}}; an entry in a style override's rules refines the limit for that package.

complexity/duplicate-function.title: CPX004: A module-level function repeats another function's code.
complexity/duplicate-function.description: A module-level function repeats another function's code. Copy-pasted helpers drift: a fix or a changed message lands in one copy and the others keep the old behavior, and readers cannot tell whether the difference is intended. This opt-in review compares module-level functions within each analyzed root package and reports every function whose parameters, annotations, decorators and body are identical to another one's, ignoring names, docstrings, comments and formatting. A body needs at least three statements, counting nested ones, so trivial one-liners are not reported. Methods, nested functions, test files and separate root packages are not compared. Each copy gets its own finding with the other locations. Repair: Keep one copy in a module both callers may import, usually in their nearest common package, and import it from there. Check architecture boundaries and import cycles when choosing the owner. Copies that must evolve independently keep a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/duplicate-function: warning}, or select CPX004.

complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.title: CPX005: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.
complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.description: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional. Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used. Repair: Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.
complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.markdownDescription:
**CPX005 — complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional**

A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.

Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used.

**Problem**
```python
status = OK if completed else TIMEOUT if timed_out else ERROR
```

**Preferred**
```python
if completed:
    status = OK
elif timed_out:
    status = TIMEOUT
else:
    status = ERROR
```

Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.

complexity/excess-comprehension-loops.title: CPX006: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps.
complexity/excess-comprehension-loops.description: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps. This opt-in syntax review reports comprehensions with too many for clauses, a conditional element/value with a nontrivial branch, or multiple filters (including a boolean filter with more than two operands). Names, attribute reads and constants are trivial branches. Nested comprehension triggers are grouped at the outermost comprehension. Simple mapping, a single filter and trivial fallbacks remain valid. Only production source is checked; no types or runtime costs are inferred. Repair: Name the per-item decision or use an explicit loop. Preserve generator laziness, iteration/filter order and conditional evaluation. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/excess-comprehension-loops: hint} or select CPX006; set max on the entry, e.g. {severity: hint, max: 2}. The limit defaults to 1; an entry in a style override's rules can permit intentional flattening.

complexity/excess-constructor-decisions.title: CPX007: A constructor contains more decisions than the configured limit.
complexity/excess-constructor-decisions.description: A constructor contains more decisions than the configured limit. Normalization, validation and derivation become easier to understand when named separately from object initialization. This opt-in review counts if, for/async for, while, try/try-star, match, raise, comprehension and conditional-expression nodes in __init__ and __post_init__ methods. Each comprehension counts once, in addition to any conditional expressions inside it; its generator clauses are not counted separately. Nested function, lambda and class definitions are skipped. Helper calls count zero. A single guard with raise counts two, so it remains valid at the default limit of 2. Only production source is checked. __new__ and other validation methods are outside the scope. This metric is advice, not proof that a constructor needs refactoring. Repair: Move a cohesive normalization or validation step into a named function or classmethod and assign its result. Preserve evaluation order, exceptions and initialization side effects. Do not extract arbitrary fragments merely to lower a count. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/excess-constructor-decisions: hint} or select CPX007; set max on the entry, in the root or a style override's rules. The limit defaults to 2; 0 forbids any counted decision. Reasoned suppressions and package off overrides are supported.

frameworks/prefer-secret-type.title: FWK001: A secret-named settings field accepts an unwrapped str or bytes value.
frameworks/prefer-secret-type.description: A secret-named settings field accepts an unwrapped str or bytes value. Pydantic SecretStr and SecretBytes mask ordinary string/repr/JSON representations. This opt-in review recognizes top-level, undecorated BaseSettings classes and same-file subclasses through stable direct import aliases. Secret names are password, passwd, secret, api_key, private_key, access_token, refresh_token and token, including underscore-delimited suffixes. It reviews str/bytes inside quoted annotations, unions, Optional and Annotated. Correct Secret types, unknown/custom types, cross-file inheritance, dynamic aliases and shadowed bindings are outside this check. Public keys, token counts and nonsecret settings remain valid. Field names are review evidence, not proof of sensitivity or absence of leaks. Defaults and secret values are never included in diagnostics. Repair: Use SecretStr for textual credentials or SecretBytes for binary credentials. Update deliberate plaintext consumers to unwrap explicitly and verify serialization. Keep nonsecret fields unchanged or suppress a misleading field name with a reason. No type annotations or consumers are rewritten automatically. Enable rules: {frameworks/prefer-secret-type: warning}; package overrides can restrict adoption.

frameworks/redundant-dishka-provider.title: FWK002: A Dishka provider method only forwards typed dependencies to a constructor.
frameworks/redundant-dishka-provider.description: A Dishka provider method only forwards typed dependencies to a constructor. Dishka can register constructors directly using provide(Implementation, provides=Interface). This opt-in review recognizes direct, undecorated Provider subclasses and synchronous @provide methods containing only one return of a class-shaped constructor call. Every typed dependency must be forwarded once, with matching keyword names or unchanged positional order. Stable direct Dishka import aliases are supported. Defaults, variadic signatures, extra decorators, mixins, async/generator/resource factories, transformations and unknown decorator options are excluded. Constructor annotations and dependency markers are not proven equivalent; the finding is a review candidate and never a graph validation or resource-ownership guarantee. Repair: Review registering the constructor directly. Verify its type hints and Dishka dependency/component markers supply the same inputs. Preserve class-level scope and explicit scope/cache/provides/override options. Keep factories with initialization logic or finalization. Suggested registrations use the canonical provide spelling; preserve the actual import alias when editing. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {frameworks/redundant-dishka-provider: hint}.

idioms/bundled-instance-assignment.title: IDM001: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.
idioms/bundled-instance-assignment.description: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention. Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error. Repair: Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. Parallel assignments, swaps, descriptors and unpacking failures can behave differently when split, so there is no automatic rewrite.


idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch.title: IDM002: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.
idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch.description: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy. Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior. Repair: Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.
idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch.markdownDescription:
**IDM002 — idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch**

Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.

Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior.

**Problem**
```python
if isinstance(event, Started):
    start(event)
elif isinstance(event, Delta | Progress):
    update(event)
elif isinstance(event, Finished) and event.ok:
    finish(event)
```

**Preferred**
```python
match event:
    case Started():
        start(event)
    case Delta() | Progress():
        update(event)
    case Finished() if event.ok:
        finish(event)
```

Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.

idioms/prefer-callable-instance.title: IDM003: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method.
idioms/prefer-callable-instance.description: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method. A class with one public instance method can express its operation through __call__ and a class name describing that operation. This opt-in design review reports one candidate per plain class with exactly one directly declared public method. Private helpers and __init__ do not count as public operations. An existing __call__ is already a callable API and is never reported. Constructor and operation signatures are reported separately, including positional-only, keyword-only and variadic arguments: construction configures the object, while __call__ must retain the method's call-time arguments and async behavior. Classes with bases, metaclass keywords, class or method decorators, additional special methods, class-level data or conditional definitions are excluded. This keeps inherited APIs, descriptors, dataclasses and explicit protocols outside this bounded syntax review. Test files are excluded. A single method does not prove a design defect: published named APIs and stateful lifecycles can justify keeping the class as it is. Dynamic monkey-patching and external API consumers are not resolved. Repair: Consider renaming the sole public method to __call__ and naming the class after its operation (for example, ReportService.generate becomes GenerateReport.__call__). Preserve the constructor signature, call-time parameters, defaults, return annotations and async behavior; do not move constructor dependencies into __call__. Review callers, dependency injection registrations and public compatibility before changing either name. No names, arguments or callers are rewritten automatically. Enable rules: {idioms/prefer-callable-instance: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select IDM003. Keep an intentional named API with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned IDM003 suppression.

idioms/redundant-name-alias.title: IDM004: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name.
idioms/redundant-name-alias.description: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name. Two names for one class or function make readers and agents ask whether they differ, and grep finds only half of the uses. Such aliases are typically compatibility names left behind by a rename or placeholders for a union that never gained a second member. This opt-in review reports unconditional module-level X = Y, X: TypeAlias = Y and type X = Y statements whose right side is a bare name or dotted attribute that refers to a class or function defined in the same module, or to an imported CapWords name. Type expressions such as unions, subscripts and Annotated, values such as constants, conditional assignments (version or import fallbacks), class-level names, typing special forms such as Any and tests are not reported. Repair: Use the target name everywhere and remove the alias. Introduce a shared name once it describes a real type expression, such as a union with a second member. Keep a deliberate public compatibility name with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/redundant-name-alias: hint}, or select IDM004.
idioms/redundant-name-alias.markdownDescription:
**IDM004 — idioms/redundant-name-alias**

A module-level name only repeats another class or function name.

Two names for one class or function make readers and agents ask whether they differ, and grep finds only half of the uses. Such aliases are typically compatibility names left behind by a rename or placeholders for a union that never gained a second member. This opt-in review reports unconditional module-level X = Y, X: TypeAlias = Y and type X = Y statements whose right side is a bare name or dotted attribute that refers to a class or function defined in the same module, or to an imported CapWords name. Type expressions such as unions, subscripts and Annotated, values such as constants, conditional assignments (version or import fallbacks), class-level names, typing special forms such as Any and tests are not reported.

**Problem**
```python
class PasswordData(BaseModel):
    username: str

AutofillData = PasswordData
```

**Preferred**
```python
class PasswordData(BaseModel):
    username: str

type AutofillData = PasswordData | CardData
```

Use the target name everywhere and remove the alias. Introduce a shared name once it describes a real type expression, such as a union with a second member. Keep a deliberate public compatibility name with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/redundant-name-alias: hint}, or select IDM004.

Run `smelt explain idioms/redundant-name-alias` for details.

idioms/missing-interface-docstring.title: IDM005: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring.
idioms/missing-interface-docstring.description: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring. A port or interface method has no implementation to read, so its docstring is the only place that states the contract: what the method guarantees, what it requires and what it leaves untouched. A bare ... body leaves implementers and callers to guess, and one undocumented member next to documented siblings usually means the contract was forgotten, not that it is obvious. This opt-in review reports @abstractmethod methods (including abstract properties) and methods of typing.Protocol classes whose body is only ..., pass or raise NotImplementedError and which have no docstring. Methods with a default implementation, @overload/@override signatures, property setters/deleters, dunder methods other than __call__ and tests are not reported. Ordinary Protocol attributes have no body and are out of scope. Repair: Replace the placeholder body with a docstring that states the method's contract; a docstring alone is a valid body, so drop the ... (Ruff PIE790 reports a placeholder left after a docstring). No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-interface-docstring: hint}, or select IDM005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

idioms/missing-broad-except-reason.title: IDM006: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything.
idioms/missing-broad-except-reason.description: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything. Catching Exception, BaseException or everything with a bare except is sometimes the right call: a background task must survive a failing callback, or a best-effort lookup may fail in many ways. Which of these applies is invisible in the code itself, and a linter pragma such as '# noqa: BLE001' or '# pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught' records only that the warning was silenced, not why. Without the reason, a reviewer cannot tell a deliberate boundary from a swallowed bug. This opt-in review reports an except clause whose type is Exception, BaseException, a tuple containing one of them, or missing, when no explanatory comment sits on the except line, on the comment lines directly above it, or between the except line and the first statement of its body, including a trailing comment on that statement. Tool directives such as noqa, pylint: disable, type: ignore, pragma: no cover and smelt: ignore do not count as an explanation, but text after them does. Handlers whose last statement is a raise and that contain no return, break or continue always propagate the failure and are not reported. Tests are not reported. Repair: Catch the specific exceptions the code can recover from. When the handler must stay broad, add a comment that states why, for example which boundary it protects or why any failure is acceptable. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-broad-except-reason: hint}, or select IDM006. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert.title: IDM007: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute.
idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert.description: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute. assert self._stack is not None in one method narrows a type for the checker. When several methods of the class repeat it, the attribute is optional in its type but required after setup, and every caller depends on a check that python -O removes. This opt-in review reports, once per class and expression, an assert of self.<attribute> is not None or isinstance(self.<attribute>, ...) that appears in at least two methods of the same class, including each operand of an and. Asserts in nested functions belong to that function, static methods are skipped and tests are not checked. Unlike a blanket assert ban, single local narrowings stay valid. Repair: Make the attribute required by constructing it before the object is used, or read it through one property or accessor that raises an error naming the missing setup step. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert: warning}, or select IDM007.

idioms/loop-invariant-collection.title: IDM008: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs.
idioms/loop-invariant-collection.description: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs. Repeated lookup-set construction can turn one validation pass into quadratic work and obscure a shared domain set. This opt-in review requires positive, file-local evidence: homogeneous immutable tuple literals, tuple[T, ...] annotations, or tuple fields of standard-library frozen dataclasses declared in the same module. Scalar projections may read directly declared fields of those frozen records. Annotations are assumed to describe standard builtin values and these concrete record types; runtime subclass overrides or frozen-state bypasses are not proved safe. This is not a runtime immutability proof. Records with bases, extra decorators or custom attribute access are excluded, as are descriptors, unknown fields and imported record types. Minimum snapshot evidence is a local @dataclass(frozen=True) record with a plain id: str field and a tuple[Record, ...] input; the outer iteration must also be a known tuple. The original Harnessed example uses Pydantic dataclasses and Annotated fields, which this initial implementation deliberately does not infer. Only direct for loops with a simple name target in functions or ordinary methods are reviewed; while and async loops are not inferred. The body must consist of passive scalar/tuple expressions, simple local assignments, conditionals, returns, breaks/continues or literal builtin error raises. Unknown calls, mutation through aliases, properties, nested loops/scopes, await/yield and uncertain operations make it stay quiet. A single-generator set comprehension must produce known builtin scalar values and appear on the right of in/not in. Equivalent projections are grouped per loop, including renamed comprehension variables. Tests are ignored. Repair: Review computing the lookup set once and reusing it. Preserve the empty-loop case, guards, exception timing and evaluation order: moving construction before a loop or guard can evaluate code that previously never ran. Keep lazy initialization at the first required check when necessary. No automatic hoisting is provided. Enable rules: {idioms/loop-invariant-collection: hint}, or select IDM008.

Scalar projections may read directly declared fields of those frozen records. Annotations are assumed to describe standard builtin values and these concrete record types; runtime subclass overrides or frozen-state bypasses are not proved safe. This is not a runtime immutability proof. Records with bases, extra decorators or custom attribute access are excluded, as are descriptors, unknown fields and imported record types. The original Harnessed example uses Pydantic dataclasses and Annotated fields, which this initial implementation deliberately does not infer. Only direct for loops with a simple name target in functions or ordinary methods are reviewed; while and async loops are not inferred. The body must consist of passive scalar/tuple expressions, simple local assignments, conditionals, returns, breaks/continues or literal builtin error raises. A single-generator set comprehension must produce known builtin scalar values and appear on the right of in/not in. Equivalent projections are grouped per loop, including renamed comprehension variables. Tests are ignored.

**Problem**
```python
def validate(wanted: tuple[str, ...], available: tuple[str, ...]):
    for name in wanted:

```

**Preferred**
```python

```

imports/excess-package-imports.title: IMP001: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.
imports/excess-package-imports.description: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, including its facade when mixed with implementation imports, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Findings include missing static exports and a cycle witness for the proposed caller/facade edges. Known cycles block bundling advice. No-cycle-found covers only explicit runtime imports; dynamic imports and implicit package initialization remain unproven. Discovered tests and conftest.py also count as outside callers, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. This does not change ARC008's separate count_tests opt-in for API expansion. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Use proposed_exports to review missing re-exports. A cycle_check of cycle blocks bundling: keep the imports or resolve dependency direction first. No automatic rewrite is performed. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.

One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.

Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. This does not change ARC008's separate count_tests opt-in for API expansion.

**Problem**

imports/excess-module-imports.title: IMP002: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows.
imports/excess-module-imports.description: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows. Many independent project dependencies can signal that a module coordinates too many responsibilities. Unlike IMP001, this review counts distinct direct target modules across every project root package, without requiring a contract on each target package. Repeated imports and multiple symbols from one module count once. Facade re-exports count at the facade path used by the caller, not at their defining modules. Standard-library and third-party imports never count; TYPE_CHECKING imports follow the existing architecture.import_graph.type_checking policy. Initializers and declared composition roots are exempt by default. This is a design hint, not proof of excessive coupling; reducing imports alone does not simplify a design. Repair: Split a cohesive responsibility into its own module or depend on deliberate package facades. Review import cycles and initializer side effects before adding re-exports. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {imports/excess-module-imports: {severity: hint, max: 15}}; max defaults to 20, zero is supported, and an entry in a style override's rules refines it for that package. module_import_exemptions defaults to [facades, composition_root]; [] checks both.

imports/forbidden-import-style.title: IMP003: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style.
imports/forbidden-import-style.description: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style. A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest style override supplies the style, else style.imports. No style is enforced without one, and this rule never changes bindings. Repair: Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. There is no automatic rewrite.

imports/prefer-package-import.title: IMP004: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import.
imports/prefer-package-import.description: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import. Importing supported names from a common package keeps callers independent of implementation paths and allows related imports to be combined. This opt-in hint requires every name in a from-import to have an unconditional, direct, same-named public re-export in an analyzed ancestor __init__.py. The nearest eligible package is suggested. Static __all__ is respected. Production imports inside that package are excluded to avoid routing its own implementation through its initializer. Discovered tests and conftest.py are checked, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. Imports in package initializers also stay unchanged. Conditional, rebound, private, star and dynamic exports, re-export chains, module imports and unscanned third-party packages are outside this check. Repair: Use the suggested package import and combine it with an existing import there when both are in the same scope and guard. Preserve aliases, comments and relative/absolute import policy. Review initializer side effects and dependency cycles. No exports are created and no automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

layout/module-docstring-convention.title: LAY002: A module docstring is missing or present against the package's module_docstrings convention.
layout/module-docstring-convention.description: A module docstring is missing or present against the package's module_docstrings convention. Repair: Add a useful module docstring before imports and other statements under require; remove or move the module introduction under forbid. Mark an intentional file exception with # smelt: ignore-file[LAY002] -- reason. No documentation is generated or deleted automatically.

layout/forbidden-private-module.title: LAY003: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy.
layout/forbidden-private-module.description: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy. Some projects use descriptive module names and keep private helpers inside them. Repair: Choose a descriptive module or package name without a leading underscore, then update imports and deliberate facade exports. A more specific package can explicitly allow the convention. layout/definition-order.title: LAY004: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries.
layout/definition-order.description: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries. Public interfaces should be easy to find. A stable topological order prioritizes configured categories while preserving category order, definition-time reads, rebinding and execution barriers. Function bodies are deferred; decorators, defaults, assignments and eager annotations are not. Future imports and declared Python 3.14+ targets defer annotations. Unions of recognized, unshadowed builtin types (and None) are modeled in eager function annotations for declared Python 3.10+ targets; imported or user-defined types and operator expressions in defaults remain unknown. Overload/property families remain atomic. Unknown execution is pinned. Attribute dictionaries of unambiguous undecorated nested functions are distinct from the enclosing ordered namespace, so vars(local_function) and local_function.__dict__ alone do not block enclosing moves. Nonlocal closure writes alone are also unrelated to module/class definition order. Unknown receivers, globals, locals, vars(), global writes and code/annotation introspection still require review. Repair: Review the expected order and execution barriers. Explicit check --fix can apply bounded moves where the package permits safe-only fixes. Imports, unknown execution and a misplaced main guard require manual review. Names and visibility are never rewritten by ordering. Refused sections identify the triggering expression and its source location in fix_blocker and fix_reason; the safety boundary stays in place. Pinned definitions are listed under coverage.ordering[].barriers with check --format json --show-coverage. Dependencies take precedence over public-first order. On Python 3.12/3.13, keep a needed annotations future import when the chosen order uses forward references; TYP002 retains it.

layout/misplaced-static-helper.title: LAY005: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function.
layout/misplaced-static-helper.description: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function. A helper that needs neither instance nor class state is often easier to find and reuse as a private module function. This package convention reviews direct sync/async methods carrying only the recognized builtin staticmethod decorator, including import aliases. Known or unresolved external same-named attribute access preserves static APIs. Classes with inheritance, subclasses or decorators, additional method decorators, special methods, __class__/super references and detected class-namespace dependencies are excluded. This is a placement preference, not proof of equivalent runtime behavior; external/dynamic consumers and definition-time dependencies still need review. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Repair: Move the helper to module scope with a leading underscore, remove @staticmethod, and update class/instance-qualified calls and callback references. Preserve annotations, defaults, evaluation order and dependencies; choose a distinct name if the module already binds it. Keep deliberate static APIs with a closest package rule set to off or reasoned suppression. No automatic extraction is performed.

layout/callee-before-caller.title: LAY006: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls.
layout/callee-before-caller.description: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls. A step-down reading order introduces a higher-level operation before its lower-level helpers. This opt-in review covers stable undecorated top-level sync/async functions and direct methods on undecorated classes without bases. It resolves direct same-module names and receiver.method calls, excludes shadowed bindings, nested scopes, comprehensions, dunder methods and recursive call components, and respects definition-time parameter/return dependencies. Only same-visibility pairs are reviewed so LAY004's public-first categories retain precedence. Dynamic lookup, inherited APIs and general call graphs are not inferred. This is a reading convention, not a correctness check. Repair: Review placing the caller before its helper within the same public/private group. Preserve defaults, decorators, annotations, rebinding and execution barriers. No definitions are reordered automatically; LAY004 independently handles public-first ordering and its bounded fixer. Enable rules: {layout/callee-before-caller: hint} or select LAY006; package overrides and reasoned suppressions apply.
