layout/misplaced-private-constant.title: LAY008: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module.
layout/misplaced-private-constant.description: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module. Implementation constants such as a controller's supported file extensions belong beside the class as private module constants when they do not form part of its object contract. This opt-in convention reports private UPPER_CASE names assigned literal scalars or recursively literal sets, lists, tuples and dictionaries in production class bodies, including annotated, chained and guarded assignments. It checks nested and local classes independently. Classes with bases, decorators or class keywords are excluded conservatively because inheritance, enums, data models and metaclasses can give attributes a class-specific contract. Public names, lowercase fields, dunder names, instance assignments, method locals, calls, comprehensions and values referring to other names are outside scope. This is a placement convention; syntax alone cannot prove that callers never override or mutate an attribute. Repair: Move the constant to the same module with a leading underscore, then update class-qualified and instance-qualified reads to use the constant name directly. Check name collisions, initialization order, name mangling, mutation, subclass overrides and external consumers before moving it. Keep intentional class contracts with a reasoned suppression or package override. Enable rules: {layout/misplaced-private-constant: error} to block the convention, or --select LAY008 to review it. No automatic move or rewrite is performed.

layout/redundant-module-name.title: LAY009: A module filename repeats context already supplied by an ancestor package.

It also recognizes a single regular trailing s (cars/car, purchase_orders/purchase_order). It does not infer irregular plurals or strip ss, us, is, ies, ses, xes, zes, ches or shes endings. Leading underscores are preserved. Substrings, names with no remaining responsibility, package names, dunder modules and separately discovered tests are outside scope. Source-root directory names are not package context. Findings are advisory because repetition may serve a published API or domain meaning. Repair: Review the shorter filename and update imports and facade exports when renaming. An occupied module/package name is not suggested. No files are renamed automatically. Enable with rules: {layout/redundant-module-name: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select LAY009. Use a package off override or a reasoned file suppression for intentional public names.

meta/missing-rule-policy.description: An explicitly enabled rule is missing the policy it needs in its scope. On full checks, it reports effective rule settings with no applicable public, min_imports_to_bundle, min_importers_to_export or import style policy for ARC007, IMP001, ARC008 or IMP003 respectively. Remove the explicit rule setting or set it to off where the convention should not apply.

meta/uncovered-package-facade.title: MET005: A package facade cannot supply names that IMP004 is enabled to check.
meta/uncovered-package-facade.description: A package facade cannot supply names that IMP004 is enabled to check. imports/prefer-package-import only reports an implementation import when an ancestor initializer already re-exports every imported name. Where the facade is empty or partial, an enabled IMP004 passes without checking anything. On full checks, this hint counts distinct outside production modules whose effective IMP004 setting is explicit and that import public names from an implementation module that no eligible facade can supply. The evidence goes to the nearest enclosing package with an initializer outside the caller; package-internal, test, initializer, private, star and facade imports do not count, and IMP004 ignore entries exclude their callers. It reports the package once its callers exceed max (default 2). A facade with its own active architecture/missing-facade-export threshold is left to that rule. Changed, staged and path-scoped checks skip this hint. Repair: Review whether to re-export these names. Re-exports can change import-time behavior. For an intentionally facade-less package, add an ignore entry for MET005 matching the package with a reason.

modeling/redundant-str-enum-value.title: MOD001: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member.
modeling/redundant-str-enum-value.description: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member. StrEnum members are already strings, so extracting .value often adds noise and loses the enum type unnecessarily. This opt-in hint recognizes direct Class.MEMBER.value reads on analyzed, top-level classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum, including import aliases, relative imports and analyzed re-exports. Simple string, auto() and member-alias declarations are supported. Ordinary Enum, str/Enum mixins, unknown or shadowed bindings, custom enum construction/value access, instance variables and dynamic lookups are excluded. Shadowing anywhere in a module conservatively limits recognition there. Repair: Prefer the member directly when the consumer accepts string subclasses. Review boundary behavior first: exact str checks, identity, repr and serialization contracts can distinguish the member from its raw value. Literal-typed parameters can also reject the member in a type checker; Smelt has no consumer type information. Keep .value or an explicit str(member) conversion where a plain string is intentional, and suppress the hint with a reason. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix.title: MOD002: A class definition carries a Base prefix or suffix instead of a responsibility.
modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix.description: A class definition carries a Base prefix or suffix instead of a responsibility. BaseService and MessageBase name a position in an inheritance hierarchy rather than the abstraction's responsibility. A responsibility-based name such as Service keeps that implementation choice out of the name. The affix does not itself create dependency coupling, and inheritance can be intentional, so this is an opt-in naming convention rather than a correctness check or an inheritance ban. It checks all class definitions in production modules, including private, nested and local classes, without inferring whether they have subclasses. After leading underscores, a prefix Base must be the whole name or be followed by an uppercase letter or underscore; a suffix Base must follow a non-empty name. Baseline, Baseball, Database and Base64 remain valid. Imports, aliases, base-class expressions, function names and test files are outside scope; inheriting from an imported BaseModel is allowed. Repair: Choose a name describing the class's responsibility or contract, then update references and deliberate exports. Preserve inheritance where it serves the design. A more specific package rule can disable the convention for compatibility, or a reasoned suppression can preserve a published name. No symbols are renamed automatically. Enable with rules: {modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix: error}, globally or in a style override, or --select MOD002.

modeling/prefer-str-enum-discriminator.title: MOD003: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields.
modeling/prefer-str-enum-discriminator.description: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields. Discriminated union variants often repeat protocol strings in Literal annotations, field defaults and dispatch code. A shared StrEnum gives those values one named definition while Literal[EventType.MEMBER] preserves each variant's narrow type. This opt-in syntax review recognizes directly annotated class fields named type, kind or tag whose typing.Literal contains exactly one raw string, with or without a default. It supports typing and typing_extensions import aliases, quoted annotations and Annotated/Required/NotRequired wrappers. Dataclasses, model classes and class-based TypedDict declarations use the same syntax. The field shape is a review candidate, not proof of union membership. Other field names, multiple-value Literals, enum-member Literals, ClassVar, type aliases, inherited fields and uncertain or shadowed typing bindings are excluded. Declared Python minima before 3.11 are excluded; unknown minima require version review. Repair: Define or reuse a shared StrEnum for the union's wire values. Keep each variant annotated as Literal[EnumType.MEMBER], and use that same member in direct defaults, dataclasses.field(default=...) or model Field(default=...). Keep explicit string values such as checkpoint.extension; auto() may change the wire contract. Review consumers and serialization before changing defaults, since exact str checks and repr can distinguish enum members. StrEnum requires Python 3.11+. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed. Suppress intentional external schema strings with a reason or disable this review for their package.

modeling/str-enum-value-convention.title: MOD004: A StrEnum spells its values against the configured auto/explicit convention.
modeling/str-enum-value-convention.description: A StrEnum spells its values against the configured auto/explicit convention. StrEnum values follow one project convention, chosen with str_enum_values. explicit (the default) keeps every value visible where it is declared, so renaming a member cannot silently change a serialized value; a member using auto() is reported. auto treats auto() as the convention because it derives the lowercased member name: an explicit string repeating that name is noise and hides which values are deliberate wire contracts. Under auto, a class with custom values such as 'mouseMoved' keeps explicit strings for every member and its auto() members are reported instead. It considers production classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum (imported as StrEnum, an alias or enum.StrEnum). Member aliases, private names and tests are ignored. Repair: Under explicit, spell each reported auto() member as its lowercased name, the value auto() produces for a StrEnum. Under auto, replace each reported explicit string with auto(), or spell the auto() members of a class with custom values explicitly. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/str-enum-value-convention: hint}, select MOD004, or set str_enum_values under style or in a style override. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

StrEnum values follow one project convention, chosen with str_enum_values. explicit (the default) keeps every value visible where it is declared, so renaming a member cannot silently change a serialized value; a member using auto() is reported. auto treats auto() as the convention because it derives the lowercased member name: an explicit string repeating that name is noise and hides which values are deliberate wire contracts. Under auto, a class with custom values such as 'mouseMoved' keeps explicit strings for every member and its auto() members are reported instead. It considers production classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum (imported as StrEnum, an alias or enum.StrEnum). Member aliases, private names and tests are ignored.

**Problem**
```python
# style: {str_enum_values: explicit}
class SignalingMessageType(StrEnum):
    DESCRIPTION = auto()
    READY = auto()
```

**Preferred**
```python
class SignalingMessageType(StrEnum):
    DESCRIPTION = "description"
    READY = "ready"
```

Under explicit, spell each reported auto() member as its lowercased name, the value auto() produces for a StrEnum. Under auto, replace each reported explicit string with auto(), or spell the auto() members of a class with custom values explicitly. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/str-enum-value-convention: hint}, select MOD004, or set str_enum_values under style or in a style override. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain modeling/str-enum-value-convention` for details.

modeling/dataclass-field-mutation.title: MOD005: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction.
modeling/dataclass-field-mutation.description: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction. A dataclass reads as a value: its generated __init__ is the constructor and its fields are what callers may rely on. When methods keep writing to self, the class is really a mutable accumulator or state machine with a value-like surface: callers can construct it in a half-built state, observe fields that are only scratch space for private helpers, and share instances whose contents change underneath them. Building the values first and passing them to a frozen dataclass, or keeping the accumulation in a plain class with private attributes, makes the lifecycle explicit. This opt-in review reports a @dataclass that is not frozen=True when a method other than __post_init__ assigns, deletes or augments an attribute of self, assigns or deletes an item of a field, calls a mutating container method such as append, add, update, pop or discard on a field declared as a mutable container, or calls setattr on self. Mutations inside nested functions of a method count. Calls that mutate through other objects, classes that are not dataclasses and tests are not reported. Intentional mutable records can keep a reasoned suppression. Repair: Compute the field values first and pass them to the constructor of a frozen dataclass, using immutable field types such as tuple, frozenset or Mapping; derive further values with properties or dataclasses.replace. When the object genuinely accumulates state, make it a plain class whose scratch attributes are private, or move the accumulation into a separate builder. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/dataclass-field-mutation: hint}, or select MOD005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

modeling/missing-dataclass-option.title: MOD006: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires.
modeling/missing-dataclass-option.description: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires. Whether a dataclass is frozen, uses slots or takes keyword-only arguments changes how callers may use it, yet codebases drift between @dataclass, @dataclass(frozen=True) and @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) without anyone being able to tell which deviations are deliberate. A style override lists dataclass_options, any of frozen, slots and kw_only, and every production @dataclass in the package must set each of them to True. An option that is missing or explicitly False is reported; a non-literal value is not judged. Missing slots is not reported when a base class comes from outside the project, such as a third-party or builtin class without __slots__, because slots save nothing there; bases from abc and typing still count. It is also not reported for classes with a functools.cached_property, which needs an instance __dict__. Nested packages can set their own list, and [] lifts the requirement. Tests are not checked. Repair: Add the missing options to the decorator. A dataclass that must stay mutable or unslotted keeps a reasoned suppression, or lives in a package whose contract sets its own dataclass_options. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {dataclass_options: [frozen, slots]}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

modeling/prefer-project-base-class.title: MOD007: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base.
modeling/prefer-project-base-class.description: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base. Projects often wrap a framework base in their own base class to share configuration, for example a pydantic BaseModel subclass that sets extra='forbid' and frozen=True. A class that inherits the framework base directly silently misses that configuration, and nothing in the class tells a reviewer. A style override maps each outside base to the project base, e.g. bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}, and production classes in the package that list the outside base among their direct bases are reported. Bases are resolved through the module's imports, including aliases and module attributes. Only inheritance is judged: importing the outside base for annotations, isinstance checks or adapters stays valid. The module that defines the project base is exempt, a nested package can set bases: {} to allow direct inheritance, and single classes can keep a reasoned suppression. Tests are not checked. Repair: Inherit the project base named in the finding and drop configuration that only repeated it. When a class deliberately needs the outside base, keep a reasoned suppression or move it into a package whose contract sets bases: {}. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

modeling/prefer-domain-exception.title: MOD008: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy.
modeling/prefer-domain-exception.description: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy. A project exception hierarchy lets callers tell a domain failure apart from a programming error. Code that keeps raising ValueError or RuntimeError for domain failures, or converts every error into one, forces callers to catch broad builtins and guess what went wrong. A style override names the project base, e.g. errors: {base: app.errors.AppError}, and production code in the package that raises a builtin exception class, with or without arguments and with or without from, is reported. NotImplementedError, StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, GeneratorExit, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit are always allowed, and errors.allow adds more, e.g. [TypeError]. Bare re-raises, raising caught or project exceptions, names that shadow a builtin, raises in protocol dunder methods such as __getattr__ or __getitem__, and pydantic validators, which must raise ValueError or AssertionError, are not reported. Tests are not checked. Repair: Raise a subclass of the configured base that names the failure, and let callers catch that subclass. When callers rely on a builtin, for example TypeError for wrong argument types, add it to errors.allow, or set errors: {} in a nested package that deliberately raises builtins. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {errors: {base: app.errors.AppError}}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

```python
except Exception as error:  # surface unreadable files
```

modeling/duplicate-class-name.title: MOD009: Two modules of one package define a public class with the same name.
modeling/duplicate-class-name.description: Two modules of one package define a public class with the same name. When two modules of the same package each define a public class called PageContent, imports, search results and review comments stop saying which one is meant, and the wrong import still type checks when the shapes are similar. This opt-in review groups public top-level classes by their nearest package, counting a package's __init__.py as part of that package, and reports every class whose name is also defined at the top level of another module there. Re-exports, private classes, nested classes, classes in separate packages and tests are not compared. Each definition gets its own finding with the other locations. Repair: Rename the classes after their role so each name says which one is meant, or merge them when they describe the same thing. A class that only exists as a private implementation detail can take a leading underscore. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/duplicate-class-name: warning}, or select MOD009.

modeling/implicit-duration-unit.title: MOD010: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number.
modeling/implicit-duration-unit.description: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number. A constant called _FRAME_TIMEOUT = 2.0 does not say whether it means seconds or milliseconds, and asyncio.timeout(2.5) at two call sites drifts apart as soon as one of them is tuned. This opt-in review reports two forms. Names (kind constant, field or parameter): module constants, class fields and function parameters whose name ends in timeout, delay, interval, duration or wait and that hold a number: an int or float annotation, possibly wrapped in Final, ClassVar, Optional, Annotated or | None, or an unannotated int or float literal. Names that end in a unit, such as _TIMEOUT_SECONDS or quiet_ms, and values typed as timedelta are valid; @overload and @override signatures are not checked. Literals (kind literal): int and float literals passed as the duration of asyncio.timeout, asyncio.sleep, asyncio.wait_for, asyncio.wait, time.sleep and the anyio and trio sleep and timeout scopes, resolved through imports and aliases, and literals added to a clock reading such as loop.time() + 10 or time.monotonic() + 10. Ruff's PLR2004 only covers comparisons. sleep(0), which yields control instead of waiting, and tests are not checked. Repair: Append the unit to the name, e.g. _SECONDS or _ms, and convert once where the value enters the code, or type the value as datetime.timedelta. Move an inline duration into a module constant or configuration field whose name states its purpose and unit, and reuse it at every call site that means the same wait. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/implicit-duration-unit: warning}, or select MOD010.

modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.title: MOD011: A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field.
modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.description: A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field. frozen=True prevents rebinding fields, but list, dict and set contents can still change, including through a reference passed to the constructor. This opt-in ownership review reports each directly annotated built-in dict, list or set instance field on a dataclass explicitly decorated with frozen=True. It resolves module/import aliases and quoted annotations, conservatively skipping names bound again anywhere in the file, local imports and wildcard imports. ClassVar, InitVar, inherited fields, wrapped/union annotations, user-defined types and type aliases are outside its scope. Non-frozen classes and tests are ignored. A Mapping annotation is a read-only interface, not proof of runtime or deep immutability. Intentional mutable reference holders can keep a reasoned field suppression. Repair: Review ownership. Use tuple or frozenset for immutable sequences/sets. For a mapping, copy before wrapping it in MappingProxyType: wrapping the caller's original dict alone still reflects alias mutations. Changing only the annotation to Mapping freezes nothing. Copying or freezing may change behavior, so no automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass: warning}, or select MOD011.
modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.markdownDescription:
**MOD011 — modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass**

A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field.

frozen=True prevents rebinding fields, but list, dict and set contents can still change, including through a reference passed to the constructor. This opt-in ownership review reports each directly annotated built-in dict, list or set instance field on a dataclass explicitly decorated with frozen=True. It resolves module/import aliases and quoted annotations, conservatively skipping names bound again anywhere in the file, local imports and wildcard imports. ClassVar, InitVar, inherited fields, wrapped/union annotations, user-defined types and type aliases are outside its scope. Non-frozen classes and tests are ignored. A Mapping annotation is a read-only interface, not proof of runtime or deep immutability. Intentional mutable reference holders can keep a reasoned field suppression.

**Problem**
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arguments:
    names: dict[str, str]
```

**Preferred**
```python
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from types import MappingProxyType

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arguments:
    names: Mapping[str, str]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "names", MappingProxyType(dict(self.names)))
```

Review ownership. Use tuple or frozenset for immutable sequences/sets. For a mapping, copy before wrapping it in MappingProxyType: wrapping the caller's original dict alone still reflects alias mutations. Changing only the annotation to Mapping freezes nothing. Copying or freezing may change behavior, so no automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass: warning}, or select MOD011.

Run `smelt explain modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass` for details.

modeling/parallel-record-fields.title: MOD012: Stored sequence fields of one instance are paired by position.
modeling/parallel-record-fields.description: Stored sequence fields of one instance are paired by position. Parallel stored sequences leave their record relationship implicit: every constructor and transformation must preserve matching positions. zip(strict=True) checks lengths but cannot check the right pairing. This opt-in design review groups zip calls over at least two distinct sequence fields on the same instance, once per class and field group, with declaration and zip locations. It checks directly declared class annotations of list, tuple, Sequence and MutableSequence, including typing spellings, quoted annotations and module/import aliases. Preceding unconditional local aliases assigned once from a receiver field are supported. Only undecorated instance methods are inspected. Rebound names, starred arguments, inherited/untyped fields, ClassVar, nested functions and unknown types are skipped. Local sequences and different receivers remain valid. Tests are ignored. The rule cannot establish that the fields form a domain record: intentional column-oriented or numerical storage is valid and can use a reasoned suppression at the reported zip site. Repair: Review whether these fields model one logical record. If so, store one sequence of named records and update construction and consumers together. Preserve length validation and iteration order. Deliberate column storage may retain a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite or correctness claim is made. Enable rules: {modeling/parallel-record-fields: hint}, or select MOD012.

tests/misplaced-test.title: TST001: A test file does not live where tests.layout expects it.
tests/misplaced-test.description: A test file does not live where tests.layout expects it. A predictable test location lets readers and agents find the tests of a module, and a test whose mirrored source no longer exists is left over from a rename or move. With `layout: mirror` the path decides: tests/billing/test_invoice.py needs app/billing/invoice.py, a package test tests/billing/test_billing.py needs app/billing/. Not every module needs a test. tests.mirror sets the convention, relative to the test root. Repair: Move or rename the file so its path mirrors the module it tests, merge it into that module's test, or list deliberately mirror_exclude tests (behaviour, integration, e2e) in tests.mirror_exclude. A missing mirrored source says nothing about whether the tested behaviour exists. Imports through package facades count as imports of the defining module. A move is suggested only when the test imports its subject (or is named exactly after it, marked `evidence: name`); otherwise `expected.candidates` lists the imported modules with their names and mirrored test paths to choose from, and two imported modules of the test's name stay undecided.

tests/private-access.title: TST002: A test imports or reads a private production name through a known module or instance.
tests/private-access.description: A test imports or reads a private production name through a known module or instance. Testing an observable public contract lets internal helpers change without rewriting tests. This opt-in convention checks imports, module-qualified accesses and direct instance reads/calls into analyzed production modules. Instance provenance comes from known production constructors (including analyzed facade re-exports), explicit annotations, and fixture returns/yields with an annotation or consistent known constructor/alias shape. Fixed tuple fixtures preserve known component types when unpacked. Unknown factories, conflicting outputs, reflection, local fakes and dunder names are excluded. Instance assignments are excluded so intentional immutability probes remain valid. A deliberate public re-export remains public. No general type inference or fixture execution is performed. Repair: Exercise the supported behavior that uses the helper. Keep a reasoned exception for a deliberate implementation/protocol test; do not expose internals solely to silence a warning. In multiline imports, place the exception on the affected imported name so formatting preserves its scope.

tests/forbidden-mock.title: TST003: A recognized mocking operation occurs in a test path that forbids mocks.
tests/forbidden-mock.description: A recognized mocking operation occurs in a test path that forbids mocks. Domain tests can exercise real domain objects and injected fakes. This opt-in path policy rejects recognized unittest.mock constructors/patching, standard pytest-mock operations and pytest.MonkeyPatch setattr/delattr replacements, including setup fixtures. MonkeyPatch setenv/delenv, mapping and directory setup are not counted as collaborator replacements. It does not infer arbitrary test doubles or traverse fixture dependencies. tests/string-patch-target.title: TST004: A recognized patch call or decorator uses a literal string target.
tests/string-patch-target.description: A recognized patch call or decorator uses a literal string target. String patch targets encode import paths that refactoring tools may not update. This opt-in convention checks unittest.mock and standard pytest-mock patch, patch.dict and patch.multiple literal targets, plus the dotted-target forms of pytest.MonkeyPatch setattr/delattr. Object/attribute forms are distinguished by their argument shape. It does not claim that object-based patching removes implementation coupling; variables and dynamically computed targets are outside this syntax check. Repair: Prefer an injected collaborator/fake. For deliberate boundary patching, use object-based patching where appropriate and patch the name looked up by the caller. No automatic rewrite is performed.

**Problem**
```python
from unittest.mock import patch
@patch("app.service.Repository")
def test_run(repository): ...
```

**Preferred**

```python
    repository = InMemoryRepository()
    run(repository)
    assert repository.saved == [42]
```

tests/excess-patches.title: TST005: A collected test exceeds its configured number of recognized patch calls.
tests/excess-patches.description: A collected test exceeds its configured number of recognized patch calls. Many replacements can indicate a test coupled to construction and internal calls. Count patch operations in decorators and the test body once per syntactic call, including patch.object. Nested helper bodies, fixtures and transitive calls are not attributed to callers. The limit is a configurable convention, not a proof that a test is bad. Repair: Reduce the scenario's dependencies or inject a fake. Keep a justified integration scenario with a reasoned exception rather than hiding patches inside helpers.

tests/missing-outcome-check.title: TST006: A collected test has no recognized explicit outcome assertion.
tests/missing-outcome-check.description: A collected test has no recognized explicit outcome assertion. A test that merely calls production code can pass when its result is wrong. This opt-in syntactic check accepts assert (except literal assert True), pytest.raises/warns/deprecated_call, unittest.TestCase assertions, known Mock/AsyncMock interaction assertion methods, awaited typed Event.wait observations bounded by wait_for or timeout contexts that raise on expiry, and configured qualified helpers. A move_on_after scope or a configured timeout helper alone does not establish outcome evidence. Mock receivers come from recognized constructors, aliases, patch results or explicit fixture annotations, never arbitrary assert_* method names. It also follows one direct call to an unambiguous, undecorated, non-generator helper in the same file, including nested helpers and async helpers explicitly awaited or passed to asyncio.run. Uncalled definitions, unexecuted coroutines, imported helper bodies, fixture execution, callbacks and further helper calls are not inferred. Possibly swallowed helper assertions supply no evidence; known raising timeout contexts retain it. It neither proves assertions execute nor judges their strength; a frozen scheduler clock can also defeat a timeout. Positive validation/smoke tests can be intentional exceptions. Checked inline Python subprocesses using an unshadowed sys.executable and literal or locally bound script text can provide direct top-level assert evidence. Dynamic scripts, files, optimized Python, shell commands and unchecked exits remain unknown; no analyzed code is executed. Repair: Assert a concrete result or observable state, check the expected exception/warning, or configure a known assertion helper. Use a reasoned exception for deliberate smoke/interaction tests. Do not add a meaningless assertion to silence the finding. helper_review gives call locations and known reasons for missing evidence: imported bodies, unexecuted local coroutines, possible swallowing, or no recognized evidence within one hop. These explain an inference boundary, not proof that a helper contains no assertions.

tests/vacuous-assertion.title: TST007: Every recognized outcome can disappear or pass trivially on empty input.
tests/vacuous-assertion.description: Every recognized outcome can disappear or pass trivially on empty input. Assertions confined to a result-dependent loop never execute if the result is empty. A positive all(...) assertion also accepts an empty collection. This opt-in review aid reports tests whose entire recognized evidence has one of these shapes, including assertions inside one directly executed same-file helper. Empty iteration inside a helper or around its call remains subject to review. Literal nonempty iteration without filters, explicit empty-result comparisons and tests with an additional independent outcome check are retained. It does not prove collection cardinality, reachability or test effectiveness, and can flag intentional universal properties over empty collections. Checked inline Python subprocesses using an unshadowed sys.executable and literal or locally bound script text can provide direct top-level assert evidence. Dynamic scripts, files, optimized Python, shell commands and unchecked exits remain unknown; no analyzed code is executed. Repair: Compare the complete result with an independent expectation, or check expected presence/cardinality before universal checks. Keep intentional empty-result cases explicit; do not add cosmetic assertions.

tests/unbounded-wait.title: TST008: A known test wait has no local deadline, or the scheduler clock is replaced.
tests/unbounded-wait.description: A known test wait has no local deadline, or the scheduler clock is replaced. A wedged subprocess or known Event.wait can hang a suite. This opt-in review aid checks subprocess.run/call/check_call/check_output and typed Popen wait/communicate calls for their own timeout, and awaited asyncio Event/Task/Future or subprocess Process waits for enclosing wait_for or timeout contexts. Async processes come from awaited create_subprocess_exec/shell factories or explicit Process annotations, including known fixture returns. Each wait/communicate needs its own guard; an earlier bounded read or a preceding kill does not bound a later exit wait. Configured qualified timeout helpers can supply guards. One direct call to an unambiguous, undecorated, non-generator same-file helper is followed, including nested helpers and async helpers explicitly awaited or passed to asyncio.run. Findings identify the operation inside that helper and its caller. An enclosing caller deadline can bound async waits but never a synchronous subprocess. Uncalled definitions, unexecuted coroutines, callbacks, imported helper bodies, further helper calls, fixture execution, external test-runner deadlines and general task flow remain outside inference. Replacing the time method on a known running asyncio loop is reported separately because deadlines on that same clock can stop too. Controlled domain clocks, positive sleeps and sleep(0) yields are not prohibited. Repair: Use a timeout at the blocking process boundary or around a known async wait. When replacing the scheduler clock, retain an independent real-time guard such as a parent-process timeout. Preserve bounded polling at real external boundaries. Findings sharing the same helper operation and diagnosis form a shared_helper presentation group with one repair and every affected test call site. JSON retains individual findings and identities; grouping does not change suppression, debt, severity totals or changed/staged scope.

**Problem**
```python
def test_import():
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'import app'], check=True)
```

**Preferred**
```python

    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'import app'], capture_output=True, timeout=10, check=False)
```

tests/independent-case-loop.title: TST009: A small literal loop repeats a candidate independent arrange/action/assert case.
tests/independent-case-loop.description: A small literal loop repeats a candidate independent arrange/action/assert case. A failure in the first independent case prevents later loop iterations from running and obscures case selection. This opt-in review aid considers top-level loops over 2-12 literal list/tuple cases with per-iteration construction/action and assertions. It excludes branches, context managers, control transfers, accumulated state, attribute writes and calls on pre-existing receivers. These exclusions preserve common replay, ownership-handoff and transaction/stream lifecycles. Independence cannot be proven syntactically; repeated calls alone and line counts are not smells. Repair: Review whether cases are independent, then use pytest.mark.parametrize with meaningful IDs. Retain loops when later actions depend on earlier state.
tests/independent-case-loop.markdownDescription:
**TST009 — tests/independent-case-loop**

A small literal loop repeats a candidate independent arrange/action/assert case.

A failure in the first independent case prevents later loop iterations from running and obscures case selection. This opt-in review aid considers top-level loops over 2-12 literal list/tuple cases with per-iteration construction/action and assertions. It excludes branches, context managers, control transfers, accumulated state, attribute writes and calls on pre-existing receivers. These exclusions preserve common replay, ownership-handoff and transaction/stream lifecycles. Independence cannot be proven syntactically; repeated calls alone and line counts are not smells.

**Problem**
```python
def test_select():
    for path in ['app/a.py', 'app/b.py']:
        selected = select(path)
        assert selected == ['app']
```

**Preferred**
```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize('path', ['app/a.py', 'app/b.py'], ids=['a', 'b'])
def test_select(path):
    assert select(path) == ['app']
```

Review whether cases are independent, then use pytest.mark.parametrize with meaningful IDs. Retain loops when later actions depend on earlier state.

tests/missing-await-assertion.title: TST010: A known async mock is checked for calls without corresponding await evidence.
tests/missing-await-assertion.description: A known async mock is checked for calls without corresponding await evidence. Calling an async mock can leave its coroutine unexecuted while call assertions still pass. This opt-in review checks direct known AsyncMock callables and explicitly async methods of known Mock/AsyncMock class specs, including aliases and consistent direct fixture returns. It accepts await assertions/history checks on the same mock and explicit negative call checks. Simple single-assignment locals can carry history values into assertions. Unknown specs, inherited or dynamically replaced methods, nested helpers and general data flow are not inferred. An AsyncMock object's arbitrary children are not assumed async. Deliberate creation/scheduling tests can assert_not_awaited or use a reasoned exception. This is evidence about an individual test, not proof that the suite misses a regression. Repair: When execution matters, check await arguments/counts or assert_awaited_once_with on this async mock. Preserve intentional scheduling tests with an explicit expectation; keep synchronous interactions unchanged.

**TST010 — tests/missing-await-assertion**

It accepts await assertions/history checks on the same mock and explicit negative call checks. Simple single-assignment locals can carry history values into assertions. Unknown specs, inherited or dynamically replaced methods, nested helpers and general data flow are not inferred. An AsyncMock object's arbitrary children are not assumed async. Deliberate creation/scheduling tests can assert_not_awaited or use a reasoned exception. This is evidence about an individual test, not proof that the suite misses a regression.

**Problem**
```python
def test_connect():
    connect = AsyncMock()
    run_handler(connect)
    connect.assert_called_once_with('account')
```

**Preferred**
```python
def test_connect():
    connect = AsyncMock()
    run_handler(connect)
    connect.assert_awaited_once_with('account')
```

tests/nondeterministic-data.title: TST011: A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator.
tests/nondeterministic-data.description: A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator. Fixed IDs and values keep ordinary test setup reproducible and make failures easier to replay. This opt-in review recognizes direct uuid1/uuid4, os.urandom, secrets and common module-level random calls, including resolved import aliases and fixture/helper bodies in analyzed test modules. It groups calls on one source line. It does not infer whether randomness is the behavior under test. Seeded Random instances and unknown generators are outside scope; module-level random calls are reviewed even if a seed was set elsewhere. Production source and test-quality exclusions are not checked. Repair: Use fixed inputs such as UUID(int=1), or an explicitly seeded local random.Random(seed) when generated variation matters. Keep tests of randomness, entropy and unique-ID behavior with a reasoned suppression. Preserve falsy-ID regression scenarios; change only incidental random setup. No source is rewritten. Enable rules: {tests/nondeterministic-data: warning} or select TST011.
tests/nondeterministic-data.markdownDescription:
**TST011 — tests/nondeterministic-data**

A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator.

Seeded Random instances and unknown generators are outside scope; module-level random calls are reviewed even if a seed was set elsewhere. Production source and test-quality exclusions are not checked.

**Problem**
```python
from uuid import uuid4

def test_create():
    lease = create(uuid4(), uuid4())
    assert lease.active
```

**Preferred**
```python
from uuid import UUID

    lease = create(UUID(int=1), UUID(int=2))

```

typing/forbidden-future-annotations.title: TYP001: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.
typing/forbidden-future-annotations.description: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy. An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically. Repair: Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. No automatic rewrite is performed.
typing/forbidden-future-annotations.markdownDescription:
**TYP001 — typing/forbidden-future-annotations**

The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.

An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically.

**Problem**
```python
from __future__ import annotations

VALUE = 1
```

**Preferred**
```python

```

Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. typing/redundant-future-annotations.title: TYP002: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need.
typing/redundant-future-annotations.description: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need. On targets before Python 3.14 or with an unknown minimum, when-needed mode retains imports for quoted and unresolved forward references, TYPE_CHECKING, runtime annotation inspection, decorated definitions and complex annotation expressions. This includes dataclasses and Pydantic models: decoration can consume annotations, so modern decorated code may receive no hint even when removal happens to work. Other cases get a conservative review hint, not proof of safe removal. Declared Python 3.14+ targets are handled by TYP001. Repair: Review whether postponement is part of the module's runtime contract, then remove unnecessary boilerplate and verify types and behavior. On Python 3.12/3.13, an annotations future import is appropriate when the chosen public-first order uses forward references; LAY004 preserves eager dependencies when the import is absent. Keep the import if it serves a real purpose; annotate a justified exception if required. Self is only an alternative for methods whose return contract follows the receiver's subclass, such as returning self or constructing cls; a matching class-name annotation alone is insufficient. No Self rewrite is suggested automatically.
typing/redundant-future-annotations.markdownDescription:
**TYP002 — typing/redundant-future-annotations**

This includes dataclasses and Pydantic models: decoration can consume annotations, so modern decorated code may receive no hint even when removal happens to work. Other cases get a conservative review hint, not proof of safe removal. Declared Python 3.14+ targets are handled by TYP001.

**Problem**
```python

def count(value: int) -> int:
    return value
```

**Preferred**

Keep the import if it serves a real purpose; annotate a justified exception if required. Self is only an alternative for methods whose return contract follows the receiver's subclass, such as returning self or constructing cls; a matching class-name annotation alone is insufficient. typing/implicit-optional-default.title: TYP003: An optional parameter with a None default uses truthiness to choose a fallback.
typing/implicit-optional-default.description: An optional parameter with a None default uses truthiness to choose a fallback. For an explicitly optional parameter, None commonly means not supplied. Using parameter or fallback also replaces valid falsy values such as zero, empty strings, empty containers and objects with custom truthiness. This opt-in review recognizes two-operand or expressions whose first operand is a directly named, unrebound parameter with a literal None default and a syntactic optional annotation (including quoted unions and typing Optional/Union/Annotated). It skips nested scopes, boolean tests, and parameters rebound anywhere in their function. Intentional falsy defaults remain valid; suppress or disable the review there. This is bounded syntax analysis, not type or control-flow inference. Repair: Review whether only None should select the fallback. If so, use parameter if parameter is not None else fallback. smelt check --select TYP003 --fix --unsafe-fixes applies this behavior-changing rewrite only to visible findings. Plain --fix leaves it unchanged. The rewrite preserves fallback laziness and source outside each expression; inline comments or explicit line continuations within an expression require manual editing. Intentional truthiness fallback should remain unchanged. Debt and changed comparisons distinguish enclosing functions, including class and nested-function names. Older debt without a function identity requires review and explicit re-recording; debt --prune does not accept it under a new function.

typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-r.title: TYP004: An @asynccontextmanager function annotates its return as AsyncIterator[T].
typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-r.description: An @asynccontextmanager function annotates its return as AsyncIterator[T]. The contextlib.asynccontextmanager decorator remains supported. Typeshed deprecates its AsyncIterator overload because the decorator consumes an async generator, including its athrow/aclose methods. Use AsyncGenerator[T, None] to express that contract explicitly; the second argument also works on Python 3.12. This opt-in check provides the same guidance without requiring a type checker. It recognizes async functions and methods with direct AsyncIterator[T] annotations from collections.abc or typing, including quoted annotations, module/import aliases and guarded module-level imports such as TYPE_CHECKING. It conservatively skips names rebound anywhere in the file, wildcard imports, local imports, re-exports, user-defined types, type aliases and wrapped annotations. Ordinary async iterators and functions already annotated as AsyncGenerator remain valid. See https://github.com/python/typeshed/blob/main/stdlib/contextlib.pyi for the deprecated overload. Repair: Replace AsyncIterator[T] with AsyncGenerator[T, None] and import AsyncGenerator from collections.abc. Preserve the yielded type and the decorator, and remove the AsyncIterator import only if unused elsewhere. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-return: warning}, or select TYP004. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.
typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-r.markdownDescription:
**TYP004 — typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-return**

An @asynccontextmanager function annotates its return as AsyncIterator[T].

The contextlib.asynccontextmanager decorator remains supported. Typeshed deprecates its AsyncIterator overload because the decorator consumes an async generator, including its athrow/aclose methods. Use AsyncGenerator[T, None] to express that contract explicitly; the second argument also works on Python 3.12. This opt-in check provides the same guidance without requiring a type checker. It recognizes async functions and methods with direct AsyncIterator[T] annotations from collections.abc or typing, including quoted annotations, module/import aliases and guarded module-level imports such as TYPE_CHECKING. It conservatively skips names rebound anywhere in the file, wildcard imports, local imports, re-exports, user-defined types, type aliases and wrapped annotations. Ordinary async iterators and functions already annotated as AsyncGenerator remain valid. See https://github.com/python/typeshed/blob/main/stdlib/contextlib.pyi for the deprecated overload.

**Problem**
```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

@asynccontextmanager
async def exclusive() -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    yield
```

**Preferred**
```python
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

@asynccontextmanager
async def exclusive() -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    yield
```

typing/prefer-deferred-annotations.title: TYP006: An annotation is quoted where deferred evaluation makes quotes unnecessary.
typing/prefer-deferred-annotations.description: An annotation is quoted where deferred evaluation makes quotes unnecessary. Quoted annotations such as list["BrowserWorkspaceTab"] are invisible to rename refactorings, read differently from their neighbors and need a decision at every forward reference. One module-level from __future__ import annotations, or a declared Python 3.14+ minimum, defers every annotation instead. This opt-in style review reports one finding per module that quotes annotations of parameters, returns or annotated assignments: on 3.14+ targets or with the future import, the quotes are redundant; otherwise the module should add the future import. Strings inside Literal and Annotated metadata are values, not annotations, and are ignored, as are quoted names in runtime expressions such as cast() or TypeVar(bound=...). A package contract with future_annotations: forbid keeps quotes on targets before 3.14. Tests are not checked. Repair: Remove the quotes; on targets before Python 3.14 add from __future__ import annotations first. The future import makes every annotation in the module a string at runtime, so verify runtime annotation consumers (dataclasses, Pydantic, FastAPI, dependency injection) and names imported only under TYPE_CHECKING. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {typing/prefer-deferred-annotations: hint}, or select TYP006.

visibility/internal-public-member.title: VIS001: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class.
visibility/internal-public-member.description: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class. An implementation helper should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in package review includes unused definitions and internally used sync/async functions and ordinary instance methods. Imports and module escapes preserve module functions; known test accesses also count as external use, leaving test-only public functions to VIS009. Explicit module __all__ exports and decorated functions are preserved. Methods on decorated, inherited or subclassed classes, special/private methods, properties and class/static methods are excluded. For methods, even unresolved same-named attribute accesses outside the owning class conservatively preserve visibility. External libraries, frameworks, dynamic reflection and unscanned callers cannot be ruled out. This finding asks for review and does not prove a rename is safe. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings preserve their public methods, including aliased re-export chains. Export evidence participates in incremental cache invalidation. Literal lazy-export tables are recognized only with a matching guarded importlib.import_module/getattr forwarder and optional globals cache. The table may supply __all__ through sorted/list/tuple. Arbitrary __getattr__, mutated/escaped tables and stubs alone do not verify runtime exports. Declared composition roots can expose entry points to a runtime and are skipped. Repair: Review the supported interface and callers. For a genuine internal helper, add a leading underscore and update calls and callback references. Resolve existing private-name collisions before renaming. Preserve deliberate public APIs with __all__ for module functions or append `# smelt: ignore[VIS001] -- <specific API reason>` to the reported definition. Keep the concrete reason beside the code; Smelt cannot verify its truth. No automatic rename is performed.

visibility/internal-public-attribute.title: VIS004: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its visibility boundary.
visibility/internal-public-attribute.description: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its visibility boundary. Implementation state should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes, including unused attributes. The default visibility boundary is the owning class. With public_attribute_boundary set to module, production reads and writes in the defining module count as internal access. Any same-named access outside the boundary conservatively preserves visibility, including unresolved receivers, writes, deletions and literal reflection. Test accesses count even when test-quality rules exclude the file; test-only reads remain the responsibility of VIS010, so these rules do not overlap. Private names, methods/properties, possible descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. This also preserves dataclass, attrs, Pydantic, NamedTuple and TypedDict data contracts. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings retain their public attributes, including aliased re-export chains. Inheritance is excluded as a whole rather than attempting to prove which fields a framework or base class owns. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages, external consumers and arbitrary dynamic access are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. This review does not prove that renaming is safe. Repair: Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore and update internal reads and writes, including same-module accesses in module mode. Check name collisions and dynamic consumers. If external callers need to read the value and writes should stay local, consider a read-only property backed by a private field. Preserve deliberate public contracts with a reasoned VIS004 suppression on the declaration or a package rule override. Suggested names avoid observed collisions. Smelt leaves renaming to the caller. Enable the rule in rules, select VIS004, or set public_attribute_boundary under style or in a style override.

visibility/foreign-private-access.title: VIS005: Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module.
visibility/foreign-private-access.description: Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module. A leading underscore marks a name as private to its owner. Reaching into a collaborator's private helpers, fields or methods couples the caller to implementation details. This opt-in review reports two kinds of access. symbol: relative and absolute from-imports and module-qualified reads of a module-level private name, through lexical import aliases, when it statically resolves to a definition in another analyzed production module, including sibling modules of the same package. Public aliases remain public, and a package initializer may re-export its own submodule's private symbol under a public alias. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking. attribute: reads, writes, calls, updates and deletes of a private member, such as self.log._images, whose receiver and defining project class are statically known and live in another module, or another package under style.private_attribute_boundary: package. Direct accesses on the method receiver to its own or inherited members are allowed. Receiver evidence comes from parameter/variable annotations, direct constructor assignments, stable local aliases, class/instance fields, property return annotations and bounded single inheritance; import aliases, relative imports and static facade re-exports resolve to the defining class. Unlike Ruff SLF001, unresolved receivers are not reported. Dunders, third-party and unknown names, private module names, reflection, same-module access, unknown factories, inherited lookup across multiple/unknown bases, arbitrary class decorators, local imports in attribute evidence, comprehension/lambda receiver bodies, closure/global-variable flow, rebound or shadowed bindings and wildcard imports are skipped. Tests are covered by tests/private-access (TST002). No control-flow narrowing, runtime dispatch or analyzed code execution is used. Repair: Give a shared helper a module-public name, keeping it out of __all__ and the package facade when it is internal to the package, or move it into the module that uses it. For attributes, expose a meaningful operation on the owning class or pass a deliberate public dependency; do not merely rename or wrap internal state to silence the report. Preserve evaluation order, exceptions and side effects. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/foreign-private-access: warning}, select VIS005, or set private_attribute_boundary under style or in a style override. The boundary defaults to module; package permits attribute cooperation between modules of the same immediate Python package and does not relax private symbols. Reasoned suppressions on the imported name, read or attribute are supported.

visibility/redundant-private-delegate.title: VIS006: A method only forwards its parameters to a private method used nowhere else.
visibility/redundant-private-delegate.description: A method only forwards its parameters to a private method used nowhere else. def events(self, *, run_id): return self._events(run_id=run_id) adds a second name and a jump without behavior: calling an async generator already defers its body until iteration, so moving the body into events behaves the same. Validation before the call is the legitimate reason for the split, so only a body consisting of one return is reported. The private method must be an undecorated method of the same class with the same parameter names and kinds, receive every parameter unchanged, and be referenced nowhere else in the module. Dunder and decorated methods, private names defined twice, classes with bases from other modules (a base may call the private hook) and tests are not reported. Subclasses in other modules that override the private method are not analyzed. Repair: Move the private method's body and async/def kind into the public method, keep the public name, signature and docstring, and delete the private method. Keep the split with a reasoned suppression when a subclass overrides the private method. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/redundant-private-delegate: hint}, or select VIS006.

Dunder and decorated methods, private names defined twice, classes with bases from other modules (a base may call the private hook) and tests are not reported. Subclasses in other modules that override the private method are not analyzed.

**Problem**
```python
class Frames:
    def events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        return self._events(run_id=run_id)

    async def _events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        async for frame in self._source(run_id):
            yield frame
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Frames:
    async def events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        async for frame in self._source(run_id):
            yield frame
```

Move the private method's body and async/def kind into the public method, keep the public name, signature and docstring, and delete the private method. Keep the split with a reasoned suppression when a subclass overrides the private method. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/redundant-private-delegate: hint}, or select VIS006.

Run `smelt explain visibility/redundant-private-delegate` for details.

visibility/excess-private-definitions.title: VIS007: A module contains more private definitions than the configured limit.
visibility/excess-private-definitions.description: A module contains more private definitions than the configured limit. A growing collection of private models and helpers can make a module's responsibility harder to understand. This opt-in review counts private classes, sync/async functions and PEP 695 type aliases directly in a production module body. A leading underscore marks privacy; dunders are excluded. Repeated declarations of the same name and kind, including overloads, count once at their first declaration. Private uppercase assignments with values are listed separately as constants and never contribute to the limit. Imports, ordinary assignment-style type aliases, methods, nested/local definitions and definitions inside control-flow statements are excluded. Package initializers are checked too. A few models beside their consumer remain valid at the default limit of 12. Even a larger cohesive model tree or parser may be intentional: this metric does not infer cohesion, separable groups or safe extraction. Repair: Review the listed definitions for a cohesive group that deserves its own module, carrying its constants and validators with it. Choose a name describing that responsibility; models.py is only one possibility. Preserve import direction, initialization, framework registration and module visibility when moving code. Do not make helpers public or extract arbitrary fragments merely to lower the count. Keep deliberate cohesive implementations with a reasoned suppression or package override. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/excess-private-definitions: hint} or select VIS007; set max on the entry, in the root or a style override's rules. The limit defaults to 12; zero is supported.

visibility/reexport-convention.title: VIS008: A package initializer spells a re-export against its configured convention.
visibility/reexport-convention.description: A package initializer spells a re-export against its configured convention. Use style.reexports to give package APIs a consistent spelling. all reports explicit same-name import aliases and uses __all__ for the public export list. alias reports ordinary imports named by a statically resolved __all__ when a same-name alias can mark the re-export. Existing aliases can coexist with an intentional runtime export list. The rule considers unique, direct import bindings in production __init__.py files. Real renames, dotted module imports, guarded or rebound names and star imports are outside its inference. Selecting the rule without a style uses all. Repair: With all, use a plain import and include the name in __all__ if it belongs to the public API. With alias, use a same-name alias such as Event as Event and preserve an intentional runtime export list. For a package that needs either spelling, set reexports to allow in a style override with a reason. This is a read-only check.
visibility/reexport-convention.markdownDescription:
**VIS008 — visibility/reexport-convention**

A package initializer spells a re-export against its configured convention.

Use style.reexports to give package APIs a consistent spelling. all reports explicit same-name import aliases and uses __all__ for the public export list. alias reports ordinary imports named by a statically resolved __all__ when a same-name alias can mark the re-export. Existing aliases can coexist with an intentional runtime export list. The rule considers unique, direct import bindings in production __init__.py files. Real renames, dotted module imports, guarded or rebound names and star imports are outside its inference. Selecting the rule without a style uses all.

**Problem**
```python
# style: {reexports: all}
# app/events/__init__.py
from .models import Event as Event
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/events/__init__.py

__all__ = ["Event"]
```

visibility/test-only-public-function.title: VIS009: A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module.
visibility/test-only-public-function.description: A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module. Leaving an internal helper public just so tests can call it enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to implementation details. This opt-in review identifies undecorated top-level sync/async functions without a leading underscore, referenced by analyzed tests and not imported or accessed by another analyzed production module. Uses inside the defining module do not justify public visibility. Aliased/relative imports and analyzed re-exports are resolved; production imports, star imports and escaped module values conservatively preserve the API. Explicit __all__ exports, dynamic export declarations, decorated functions, rebound names, methods and nested functions are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence. External consumers, packaging entry points and arbitrary dynamic access are not fully known; a finding is a review candidate, not proof that a function can be made private safely. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), packages outside source selection and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent. Findings expose the configured usage_scope. When no references exist inside the defining module either, the finding says unused outside tests among analyzed modules and lists the internal reference evidence. This is not proof of dead code for unassessed consumers. Repair: If this is an internal helper, add a leading underscore and update internal references. Prefer testing the public behavior that calls it. If direct helper tests are deliberate, keep a reasoned private-access exception; if it is a supported external API, declare it in __all__ or document a reasoned suppression. Review callers before renaming.

Explicit __all__ exports, dynamic export declarations, decorated functions, rebound names, methods and nested functions are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence. External consumers, packaging entry points and arbitrary dynamic access are not fully known; a finding is a review candidate, not proof that a function can be made private safely. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), packages outside source selection and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent. Findings expose the configured usage_scope. When no references exist inside the defining module either, the finding says unused outside tests among analyzed modules and lists the internal reference evidence. This is not proof of dead code for unassessed consumers.

**Problem**

```python
__all__ = ['drag']
async def drag_gesture(tab): ...
async def drag(tab):

# tests/test_mouse.py
```

visibility/test-only-public-attribute.title: VIS010: Tests read a public attribute with no observed production access outside its visibility boundary.
visibility/test-only-public-attribute.description: Tests read a public attribute with no observed production access outside its visibility boundary. Exposing implementation state just for tests enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to internal representation. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes. Reads by analyzed tests are resolved through known constructors, annotations, fixtures and class aliases/re-exports. The owning class is the default visibility boundary. With public_attribute_boundary set to module, production code in the defining module counts as internal. Any same-named production attribute access outside the boundary, including unresolved receivers and literal reflection, conservatively preserves visibility. Private names, methods/properties, descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence; test writes alone do not trigger a finding. External consumers and arbitrary dynamic access remain unknown, so renaming requires review. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. Public attributes of classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings are treated as supported API and retained, including aliased re-export chains. Repair: Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore, update internal references and test observable public behavior. Keep deliberate external or framework contracts with a reasoned suppression. Suggested names avoid observed collisions. Smelt leaves renaming to the caller.
visibility/test-only-public-attribute.markdownDescription:
**VIS010 — visibility/test-only-public-attribute**

Tests read a public attribute with no observed production access outside its visibility boundary.

Exposing implementation state just for tests enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to internal representation. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes. Reads by analyzed tests are resolved through known constructors, annotations, fixtures and class aliases/re-exports. The owning class is the default visibility boundary. With public_attribute_boundary set to module, production code in the defining module counts as internal. Any same-named production attribute access outside the boundary, including unresolved receivers and literal reflection, conservatively preserves visibility. Private names, methods/properties, descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence; test writes alone do not trigger a finding. External consumers and arbitrary dynamic access remain unknown, so renaming requires review. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. Public attributes of classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings are treated as supported API and retained, including aliased re-export chains.

**Problem**
```python
class Worker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pending = []
    def run(self):
        self.pending.clear()
# tests/test_worker.py
from app.worker import Worker
def test_run():
    worker = Worker()
    worker.run()
    assert worker.pending == []
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Worker:
    def __init__(self):
        self._pending = []
    def run(self):
        self._pending.clear()
        return 'done'
# tests/test_worker.py
from app.worker import Worker
def test_run():
    assert Worker().run() == 'done'
```

Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore, update internal references and test observable public behavior. Keep deliberate external or framework contracts with a reasoned suppression. Suggested names avoid observed collisions. Smelt leaves renaming to the caller.

Run `smelt explain visibility/test-only-public-attribute` for details.

^ARC001$.title: ARC001: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
^ARC001$.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.
^ARC001$.markdownDescription:
**ARC001 — architecture/layer-boundary**

A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.

Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import SqlVoiceSessionRepository
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.ports import VoiceSessionRepository

# gateway/bootstrap.py wires SqlVoiceSessionRepository to the port
```

Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain architecture/layer-boundary` for details.

^ARC002$.title: ARC002: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
^ARC002$.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

^ARC003$.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.
