^ARC004$.title: ARC004: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.
^ARC004$.description: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (ARC001, ARC002, ARC006) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.
^ARC004$.markdownDescription:
**ARC004 — architecture/import-cycle**

Imports that other rules already forbid (ARC001, ARC002, ARC006) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained.

**Problem**


^ARC005$.title: ARC005: A shared or central module imports a feature module.

^ARC008$.title: ARC008: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.
^ARC008$.description: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export. A contract's min_importers_to_export threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional architecture.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before. Repair: Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. Dynamic imports, implicit package initialization and import order are not proven. No exports, imports or policy are rewritten automatically.
^ARC008$.markdownDescription:
**ARC008 — architecture/missing-facade-export**

A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.

A contract's min_importers_to_export threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional architecture.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before.

**Problem**

```python
# Three outside modules each use:

```

**Preferred**

^ARC009$.title: ARC009: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist.
^ARC009$.description: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist. Member-local layers describe internal design; workspace member boundaries describe which projects may depend on one another. Only direct production imports between discovered members count. Unmatched source members are unrestricted, overlapping source globs combine their allowances, and imports inside one member always pass. Wiring and shared modules retain these boundaries. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply. Repair: Move the dependency to an allowed member or invert it behind an interface; change the root allowlist only if the dependency belongs in the intended design.
^ARC009$.markdownDescription:
**ARC009 — architecture/member-boundary**

A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist.

Member-local layers describe internal design; workspace member boundaries describe which projects may depend on one another. Only direct production imports between discovered members count. Unmatched source members are unrestricted, overlapping source globs combine their allowances, and imports inside one member always pass. Wiring and shared modules retain these boundaries. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply.

**Problem**
```python
# packages/core/src/core/model.py
from api.http import serve
# root policy: architecture.members: {'packages/*': {may_depend_on: []}}
```

**Preferred**
```python
# services/api/src/api/http.py

# root policy: architecture.members: {'services/*': {may_depend_on: ['packages/*']}}
```

Move the dependency to an allowed member or invert it behind an interface; change the root allowlist only if the dependency belongs in the intended design.

Run `smelt explain architecture/member-boundary` for details.

^ARC010$.title: ARC010: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency.
^ARC010$.description: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency. One shared import graph makes undeclared imports work locally, but the member may fail when installed independently. This rule compares direct production imports with project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and tool.uv.sources. Distribution names are normalized independently of Python package names. Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations. Repair: For an allowed dependency, declare the imported member's distribution in project.dependencies and configure its uv workspace source. If architecture.members forbids the dependency, remove the import or move the dependency behind an allowed member boundary.
^ARC010$.markdownDescription:
**ARC010 — architecture/undeclared-member-dependency**

A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency.

One shared import graph makes undeclared imports work locally, but the member may fail when installed independently. This rule compares direct production imports with project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and tool.uv.sources. Distribution names are normalized independently of Python package names. Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations.

**Problem**
```toml
[project]
name = "api"
dependencies = []
# api imports core.model
```

**Preferred**
```toml
[project]
name = "api"
dependencies = ["core-lib"]
[tool.uv.sources]
core-lib = {workspace = true}
```

^CPX001$.title: CPX001: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes.
^CPX001$.description: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes. An instance method that reaches through several stored collaborators depends on their internal arrangement. This opt-in Law of Demeter review reports calls with at least two consecutive attribute accesses from the instance receiver before the first method call, such as self.browser.input.motor(). One finding covers a whole receiver call chain. Direct collaborator calls, pure data reads and fluent chains starting from a direct collaborator are excluded. Module objects stored from unshadowed imports or declared as ModuleType, explicit SimpleNamespace trees, and typed dataclass/Pydantic record paths ending in known containers or values are namespaces rather than collaborator graphs. Known pathlib parent paths and subprocess pipes also retain their standard APIs. Namespace evidence comes from annotations, direct constructor assignments and property return annotations; analyzed imports and re-exports are followed without executing code. Every intermediate object must be a known namespace or value: a record containing a service does not exempt navigation into that service. Names such as api, client, get or append alone exempt nothing. Unknown SDK types and dynamic property/data flow remain review limitations. Decorated and implicit class/static methods, nested helper bodies, comprehensions, receiver rebinding and navigation through parameters, aliases or subscripts are outside the review. This is a bounded review, not proof of a design defect. When namespace evidence is incomplete, the finding includes the declared/constructed root type and the unresolved step. These are review inputs for an agent, not proof that the API is poorly designed. Inspect the public API contract before choosing a refactor; an intentional namespace can be a valid conclusion. Repair: Review whether the caller should receive the needed collaborator directly or ask its direct collaborator to perform the operation. A local variable alone does not reduce structural coupling. Preserve factory/property evaluation and object lifetimes; repeated lookups need not return the same object. Keep intentional API navigation with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned CPX001 suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable with rules: {complexity/excess-attribute-depth: hint}, globally or in a package override, or --select CPX001.

^CPX002$.title: CPX002: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.
^CPX002$.description: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument. Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded. Repair: Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.
^CPX002$.markdownDescription:
**CPX002 — complexity/inline-call-argument**

An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.

Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded.

**Problem**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    return Response(
        text=await browser.clipboard.read(),
        users=[to_user(user) for user in result.users],
        active=sum(user.active for user in result.users),
    )
```

**Preferred**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    text = await browser.clipboard.read()
    users = [to_user(user) for user in result.users]
    active = sum(user.active for user in result.users)
    return Response(text=text, users=users, active=active)
```

Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain complexity/inline-call-argument` for details.

^CPX003$.title: CPX003: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows.
^CPX003$.description: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows. Call sites such as connect(user, run, tab, True) do not say which value is which, and swapping two arguments of the same type still type-checks. The max of the rule entry is the limit (5 when omitted); parameters after that limit must be keyword-only so every call names them. self and cls are not counted, nor are *args and **kwargs. Dunder methods, @overload and @override definitions are exempt because their signatures are dictated elsewhere, and tests are not checked. Positional-only parameters count like any other positional parameter. Repair: Insert * after the last allowed positional parameter, then pass the remaining arguments by keyword at every call site. Callbacks whose positional signature is fixed by a framework keep it with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {complexity/excess-positional-parameters: {severity: warning, max: 3}}; an entry in a style override's rules refines the limit for that package.
^CPX003$.markdownDescription:
**CPX003 — complexity/excess-positional-parameters**

A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows.

Call sites such as connect(user, run, tab, True) do not say which value is which, and swapping two arguments of the same type still type-checks. The max of the rule entry is the limit (5 when omitted); parameters after that limit must be keyword-only so every call names them. self and cls are not counted, nor are *args and **kwargs. Dunder methods, @overload and @override definitions are exempt because their signatures are dictated elsewhere, and tests are not checked. Positional-only parameters count like any other positional parameter.

**Problem**
```python

    ...
```

**Preferred**

Callbacks whose positional signature is fixed by a framework keep it with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. ^CPX004$.title: CPX004: A module-level function repeats another function's code.
^CPX004$.description: A module-level function repeats another function's code. Copy-pasted helpers drift: a fix or a changed message lands in one copy and the others keep the old behavior, and readers cannot tell whether the difference is intended. This opt-in review compares module-level functions within each analyzed root package and reports every function whose parameters, annotations, decorators and body are identical to another one's, ignoring names, docstrings, comments and formatting. A body needs at least three statements, counting nested ones, so trivial one-liners are not reported. Methods, nested functions, test files and separate root packages are not compared. Each copy gets its own finding with the other locations. Repair: Keep one copy in a module both callers may import, usually in their nearest common package, and import it from there. Check architecture boundaries and import cycles when choosing the owner. Copies that must evolve independently keep a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/duplicate-function: warning}, or select CPX004.

^CPX005$.title: CPX005: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.
^CPX005$.description: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional. Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used. Repair: Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.
^CPX005$.markdownDescription:
**CPX005 — complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional**

A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.

Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used.

**Problem**
```python
status = OK if completed else TIMEOUT if timed_out else ERROR
```

**Preferred**
```python
if completed:
    status = OK
elif timed_out:
    status = TIMEOUT
else:
    status = ERROR
```

Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional` for details.

^CPX006$.title: CPX006: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps.
^CPX006$.description: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps. This opt-in syntax review reports comprehensions with too many for clauses, a conditional element/value with a nontrivial branch, or multiple filters (including a boolean filter with more than two operands). Names, attribute reads and constants are trivial branches. Nested comprehension triggers are grouped at the outermost comprehension. Simple mapping, a single filter and trivial fallbacks remain valid. Only production source is checked; no types or runtime costs are inferred. Repair: Name the per-item decision or use an explicit loop. Preserve generator laziness, iteration/filter order and conditional evaluation. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/excess-comprehension-loops: hint} or select CPX006; set max on the entry, e.g. {severity: hint, max: 2}. The limit defaults to 1; an entry in a style override's rules can permit intentional flattening.
^CPX006$.markdownDescription:
**CPX006 — complexity/excess-comprehension-loops**

A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps.

This opt-in syntax review reports comprehensions with too many for clauses, a conditional element/value with a nontrivial branch, or multiple filters (including a boolean filter with more than two operands). Names, attribute reads and constants are trivial branches. Nested comprehension triggers are grouped at the outermost comprehension. Simple mapping, a single filter and trivial fallbacks remain valid. Only production source is checked; no types or runtime costs are inferred.

**Problem**
```python
values = [convert(x) if x.ready else fallback(x) for x in items]
```

**Preferred**
```python
values = [resolve_item(x) for x in items]
```

^CPX007$.description: A constructor contains more decisions than the configured limit. ^IDM001$.title: IDM001: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.
^IDM001$.description: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention. Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error. Repair: Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. ^IDM002$.title: IDM002: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.
^IDM002$.description: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy. Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior. Repair: Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.

^IDM003$.title: IDM003: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method.
^IDM003$.description: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method. A class with one public instance method can express its operation through __call__ and a class name describing that operation. This opt-in design review reports one candidate per plain class with exactly one directly declared public method. Private helpers and __init__ do not count as public operations. An existing __call__ is already a callable API and is never reported. Constructor and operation signatures are reported separately, including positional-only, keyword-only and variadic arguments: construction configures the object, while __call__ must retain the method's call-time arguments and async behavior. Classes with bases, metaclass keywords, class or method decorators, additional special methods, class-level data or conditional definitions are excluded. This keeps inherited APIs, descriptors, dataclasses and explicit protocols outside this bounded syntax review. Test files are excluded. A single method does not prove a design defect: published named APIs and stateful lifecycles can justify keeping the class as it is. Dynamic monkey-patching and external API consumers are not resolved. Repair: Consider renaming the sole public method to __call__ and naming the class after its operation (for example, ReportService.generate becomes GenerateReport.__call__). Preserve the constructor signature, call-time parameters, defaults, return annotations and async behavior; do not move constructor dependencies into __call__. Review callers, dependency injection registrations and public compatibility before changing either name. No names, arguments or callers are rewritten automatically. Enable rules: {idioms/prefer-callable-instance: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select IDM003. Keep an intentional named API with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned IDM003 suppression.

^IDM004$.title: IDM004: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name.
^IDM004$.description: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name. Two names for one class or function make readers and agents ask whether they differ, and grep finds only half of the uses. Such aliases are typically compatibility names left behind by a rename or placeholders for a union that never gained a second member. This opt-in review reports unconditional module-level X = Y, X: TypeAlias = Y and type X = Y statements whose right side is a bare name or dotted attribute that refers to a class or function defined in the same module, or to an imported CapWords name. Type expressions such as unions, subscripts and Annotated, values such as constants, conditional assignments (version or import fallbacks), class-level names, typing special forms such as Any and tests are not reported. Repair: Use the target name everywhere and remove the alias. Introduce a shared name once it describes a real type expression, such as a union with a second member. Keep a deliberate public compatibility name with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/redundant-name-alias: hint}, or select IDM004.

^IDM005$.title: IDM005: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring.
^IDM005$.description: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring. A port or interface method has no implementation to read, so its docstring is the only place that states the contract: what the method guarantees, what it requires and what it leaves untouched. A bare ... body leaves implementers and callers to guess, and one undocumented member next to documented siblings usually means the contract was forgotten, not that it is obvious. This opt-in review reports @abstractmethod methods (including abstract properties) and methods of typing.Protocol classes whose body is only ..., pass or raise NotImplementedError and which have no docstring. Methods with a default implementation, @overload/@override signatures, property setters/deleters, dunder methods other than __call__ and tests are not reported. Ordinary Protocol attributes have no body and are out of scope. Repair: Replace the placeholder body with a docstring that states the method's contract; a docstring alone is a valid body, so drop the ... (Ruff PIE790 reports a placeholder left after a docstring). No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-interface-docstring: hint}, or select IDM005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

^IDM006$.title: IDM006: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything.
^IDM006$.description: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything. Catching Exception, BaseException or everything with a bare except is sometimes the right call: a background task must survive a failing callback, or a best-effort lookup may fail in many ways. Which of these applies is invisible in the code itself, and a linter pragma such as '# noqa: BLE001' or '# pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught' records only that the warning was silenced, not why. Without the reason, a reviewer cannot tell a deliberate boundary from a swallowed bug. This opt-in review reports an except clause whose type is Exception, BaseException, a tuple containing one of them, or missing, when no explanatory comment sits on the except line, on the comment lines directly above it, or between the except line and the first statement of its body, including a trailing comment on that statement. Tool directives such as noqa, pylint: disable, type: ignore, pragma: no cover and smelt: ignore do not count as an explanation, but text after them does. Handlers whose last statement is a raise and that contain no return, break or continue always propagate the failure and are not reported. Tests are not reported. Repair: Catch the specific exceptions the code can recover from. When the handler must stay broad, add a comment that states why, for example which boundary it protects or why any failure is acceptable. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-broad-except-reason: hint}, or select IDM006. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.
^IDM006$.markdownDescription:

^IDM007$.title: IDM007: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute.
^IDM007$.description: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute. assert self._stack is not None in one method narrows a type for the checker. When several methods of the class repeat it, the attribute is optional in its type but required after setup, and every caller depends on a check that python -O removes. This opt-in review reports, once per class and expression, an assert of self.<attribute> is not None or isinstance(self.<attribute>, ...) that appears in at least two methods of the same class, including each operand of an and. Asserts in nested functions belong to that function, static methods are skipped and tests are not checked. Unlike a blanket assert ban, single local narrowings stay valid. Repair: Make the attribute required by constructing it before the object is used, or read it through one property or accessor that raises an error naming the missing setup step. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert: warning}, or select IDM007.

^IDM008$.title: IDM008: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs.
^IDM008$.description: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs. Repeated lookup-set construction can turn one validation pass into quadratic work and obscure a shared domain set. This opt-in review requires positive, file-local evidence: homogeneous immutable tuple literals, tuple[T, ...] annotations, or tuple fields of standard-library frozen dataclasses declared in the same module. Scalar projections may read directly declared fields of those frozen records. Annotations are assumed to describe standard builtin values and these concrete record types; runtime subclass overrides or frozen-state bypasses are not proved safe. This is not a runtime immutability proof. Records with bases, extra decorators or custom attribute access are excluded, as are descriptors, unknown fields and imported record types. Preserve the empty-loop case, guards, exception timing and evaluation order: moving construction before a loop or guard can evaluate code that previously never ran. Keep lazy initialization at the first required check when necessary. No automatic hoisting is provided. Enable rules: {idioms/loop-invariant-collection: hint}, or select IDM008.

^IMP001$.title: IMP001: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.
^IMP001$.description: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. Discovered tests and conftest.py also count as outside callers, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. This does not change ARC008's separate count_tests opt-in for API expansion. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Use proposed_exports to review missing re-exports. A cycle_check of cycle blocks bundling: keep the imports or resolve dependency direction first. No automatic rewrite is performed. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.

^IMP002$.title: IMP002: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows.
^IMP002$.description: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows. Many independent project dependencies can signal that a module coordinates too many responsibilities. Repeated imports and multiple symbols from one module count once. Facade re-exports count at the facade path used by the caller, not at their defining modules. ^IMP004$.description: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import. Static __all__ is respected. Production imports inside that package are excluded to avoid routing its own implementation through its initializer. Discovered tests and conftest.py are checked, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. Imports in package initializers also stay unchanged. ^LAY004$.title: LAY004: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries.
^LAY004$.description: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries. Public interfaces should be easy to find. A stable topological order prioritizes configured categories while preserving category order, definition-time reads, rebinding and execution barriers. Function bodies are deferred; decorators, defaults, assignments and eager annotations are not. Future imports and declared Python 3.14+ targets defer annotations. Unions of recognized, unshadowed builtin types (and None) are modeled in eager function annotations for declared Python 3.10+ targets; imported or user-defined types and operator expressions in defaults remain unknown. Overload/property families remain atomic. Unknown execution is pinned. Attribute dictionaries of unambiguous undecorated nested functions are distinct from the enclosing ordered namespace, so vars(local_function) and local_function.__dict__ alone do not block enclosing moves. Nonlocal closure writes alone are also unrelated to module/class definition order. Unknown receivers, globals, locals, vars(), global writes and code/annotation introspection still require review. Repair: Review the expected order and execution barriers. Explicit check --fix can apply bounded moves where the package permits safe-only fixes. Imports, unknown execution and a misplaced main guard require manual review. Names and visibility are never rewritten by ordering. Refused sections identify the triggering expression and its source location in fix_blocker and fix_reason; the safety boundary stays in place. Pinned definitions are listed under coverage.ordering[].barriers with check --format json --show-coverage. Dependencies take precedence over public-first order. On Python 3.12/3.13, keep a needed annotations future import when the chosen order uses forward references; TYP002 retains it.

^LAY005$.title: LAY005: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function.
^LAY005$.description: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function. A helper that needs neither instance nor class state is often easier to find and reuse as a private module function. This package convention reviews direct sync/async methods carrying only the recognized builtin staticmethod decorator, including import aliases. Known or unresolved external same-named attribute access preserves static APIs. Classes with inheritance, subclasses or decorators, additional method decorators, special methods, __class__/super references and detected class-namespace dependencies are excluded. This is a placement preference, not proof of equivalent runtime behavior; external/dynamic consumers and definition-time dependencies still need review. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Repair: Move the helper to module scope with a leading underscore, remove @staticmethod, and update class/instance-qualified calls and callback references. Preserve annotations, defaults, evaluation order and dependencies; choose a distinct name if the module already binds it. Keep deliberate static APIs with a closest package rule set to off or reasoned suppression. No automatic extraction is performed.

^LAY006$.title: LAY006: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls.
^LAY006$.description: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls. A step-down reading order introduces a higher-level operation before its lower-level helpers. This opt-in review covers stable undecorated top-level sync/async functions and direct methods on undecorated classes without bases. It resolves direct same-module names and receiver.method calls, excludes shadowed bindings, nested scopes, comprehensions, dunder methods and recursive call components, and respects definition-time parameter/return dependencies. Only same-visibility pairs are reviewed so LAY004's public-first categories retain precedence. Dynamic lookup, inherited APIs and general call graphs are not inferred. This is a reading convention, not a correctness check. Repair: Review placing the caller before its helper within the same public/private group. Preserve defaults, decorators, annotations, rebinding and execution barriers. No definitions are reordered automatically; LAY004 independently handles public-first ordering and its bounded fixer. Enable rules: {layout/callee-before-caller: hint} or select LAY006; package overrides and reasoned suppressions apply.

^LAY007$.title: LAY007: A YAML or Compose filename differs from the project's canonical spelling.
^LAY007$.description: A YAML or Compose filename differs from the project's canonical spelling. A file violating both options gets one finding with the fully corrected path. Custom filenames such as stack.yaml are not classified by content. Project exclusions and tool/cache directories are skipped. No YAML contents are parsed, and an omitted option permits either spelling even with --select ALL. Repair: Rename the file to the expected path and update references to its old name, including CI, scripts, docker compose -f arguments and extends entries. Check for existing destination files before renaming. No file or reference is changed automatically. Use a reasoned project.exclude or ignore.paths entry for filenames required by another tool.

^LAY008$.title: LAY008: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module.
^LAY008$.description: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module. Implementation constants such as a controller's supported file extensions belong beside the class as private module constants when they do not form part of its object contract. This opt-in convention reports private UPPER_CASE names assigned literal scalars or recursively literal sets, lists, tuples and dictionaries in production class bodies, including annotated, chained and guarded assignments. It checks nested and local classes independently. Classes with bases, decorators or class keywords are excluded conservatively because inheritance, enums, data models and metaclasses can give attributes a class-specific contract. Public names, lowercase fields, dunder names, instance assignments, method locals, calls, comprehensions and values referring to other names are outside scope. This is a placement convention; syntax alone cannot prove that callers never override or mutate an attribute. Repair: Move the constant to the same module with a leading underscore, then update class-qualified and instance-qualified reads to use the constant name directly. No automatic move or rewrite is performed.

Enable with rules: {layout/redundant-module-name: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select LAY009. Use a package off override or a reasoned file suppression for intentional public names.

^MOD004$.title: MOD004: A StrEnum spells its values against the configured auto/explicit convention.

^MOD005$.title: MOD005: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction.
^MOD005$.description: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction. A dataclass reads as a value: its generated __init__ is the constructor and its fields are what callers may rely on. When methods keep writing to self, the class is really a mutable accumulator or state machine with a value-like surface: callers can construct it in a half-built state, observe fields that are only scratch space for private helpers, and share instances whose contents change underneath them. Building the values first and passing them to a frozen dataclass, or keeping the accumulation in a plain class with private attributes, makes the lifecycle explicit. This opt-in review reports a @dataclass that is not frozen=True when a method other than __post_init__ assigns, deletes or augments an attribute of self, assigns or deletes an item of a field, calls a mutating container method such as append, add, update, pop or discard on a field declared as a mutable container, or calls setattr on self. Mutations inside nested functions of a method count. Calls that mutate through other objects, classes that are not dataclasses and tests are not reported. Intentional mutable records can keep a reasoned suppression. Repair: Compute the field values first and pass them to the constructor of a frozen dataclass, using immutable field types such as tuple, frozenset or Mapping; derive further values with properties or dataclasses.replace. When the object genuinely accumulates state, make it a plain class whose scratch attributes are private, or move the accumulation into a separate builder. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/dataclass-field-mutation: hint}, or select MOD005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

^MOD006$.title: MOD006: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires.
^MOD006$.description: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires. Whether a dataclass is frozen, uses slots or takes keyword-only arguments changes how callers may use it, yet codebases drift between @dataclass, @dataclass(frozen=True) and @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) without anyone being able to tell which deviations are deliberate. A style override lists dataclass_options, any of frozen, slots and kw_only, and every production @dataclass in the package must set each of them to True. An option that is missing or explicitly False is reported; a non-literal value is not judged. Missing slots is not reported when a base class comes from outside the project, such as a third-party or builtin class without __slots__, because slots save nothing there; bases from abc and typing still count. It is also not reported for classes with a functools.cached_property, which needs an instance __dict__. Nested packages can set their own list, and [] lifts the requirement. Tests are not checked. Repair: Add the missing options to the decorator. A dataclass that must stay mutable or unslotted keeps a reasoned suppression, or lives in a package whose contract sets its own dataclass_options. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {dataclass_options: [frozen, slots]}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

^MOD007$.title: MOD007: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base.
^MOD007$.description: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base. Projects often wrap a framework base in their own base class to share configuration, for example a pydantic BaseModel subclass that sets extra='forbid' and frozen=True. A class that inherits the framework base directly silently misses that configuration, and nothing in the class tells a reviewer. A style override maps each outside base to the project base, e.g. bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}, and production classes in the package that list the outside base among their direct bases are reported. Bases are resolved through the module's imports, including aliases and module attributes. Only inheritance is judged: importing the outside base for annotations, isinstance checks or adapters stays valid. The module that defines the project base is exempt, a nested package can set bases: {} to allow direct inheritance, and single classes can keep a reasoned suppression. Tests are not checked. Repair: Inherit the project base named in the finding and drop configuration that only repeated it. When a class deliberately needs the outside base, keep a reasoned suppression or move it into a package whose contract sets bases: {}. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

^MOD008$.title: MOD008: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy.
^MOD008$.description: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy. A project exception hierarchy lets callers tell a domain failure apart from a programming error. Code that keeps raising ValueError or RuntimeError for domain failures, or converts every error into one, forces callers to catch broad builtins and guess what went wrong. A style override names the project base, e.g. errors: {base: app.errors.AppError}, and production code in the package that raises a builtin exception class, with or without arguments and with or without from, is reported. ^MOD010$.title: MOD010: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number.
^MOD010$.description: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number. A constant called _FRAME_TIMEOUT = 2.0 does not say whether it means seconds or milliseconds, and asyncio.timeout(2.5) at two call sites drifts apart as soon as one of them is tuned. This opt-in review reports two forms. Names (kind constant, field or parameter): module constants, class fields and function parameters whose name ends in timeout, delay, interval, duration or wait and that hold a number: an int or float annotation, possibly wrapped in Final, ClassVar, Optional, Annotated or | None, or an unannotated int or float literal. Names that end in a unit, such as _TIMEOUT_SECONDS or quiet_ms, and values typed as timedelta are valid; @overload and @override signatures are not checked. Literals (kind literal): int and float literals passed as the duration of asyncio.timeout, asyncio.sleep, asyncio.wait_for, asyncio.wait, time.sleep and the anyio and trio sleep and timeout scopes, resolved through imports and aliases, and literals added to a clock reading such as loop.time() + 10 or time.monotonic() + 10. Ruff's PLR2004 only covers comparisons. sleep(0), which yields control instead of waiting, and tests are not checked. Repair: Append the unit to the name, e.g. _SECONDS or _ms, and convert once where the value enters the code, or type the value as datetime.timedelta. Move an inline duration into a module constant or configuration field whose name states its purpose and unit, and reuse it at every call site that means the same wait. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/implicit-duration-unit: warning}, or select MOD010.

^TST001$.description: A test file does not live where tests.layout expects it. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings retain their public attributes, including aliased re-export chains. Inheritance is excluded as a whole rather than attempting to prove which fields a framework or base class owns. Implementation state should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. The default visibility boundary is the owning class. With public_attribute_boundary set to module, production reads and writes in the defining module count as internal access. ^VIS005$.description: Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module. A leading underscore marks a name as private to its owner. Public aliases remain public, and a package initializer may re-export its own submodule's private symbol under a public alias. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking. attribute: reads, writes, calls, updates and deletes of a private member, such as self.log._images, whose receiver and defining project class are statically known and live in another module, or another package under style.private_attribute_boundary: package. ^VIS006$.title: VIS006: A method only forwards its parameters to a private method used nowhere else.
^VIS006$.description: A method only forwards its parameters to a private method used nowhere else. def events(self, *, run_id): return self._events(run_id=run_id) adds a second name and a jump without behavior: calling an async generator already defers its body until iteration, so moving the body into events behaves the same. Validation before the call is the legitimate reason for the split, so only a body consisting of one return is reported. The private method must be an undecorated method of the same class with the same parameter names and kinds, receive every parameter unchanged, and be referenced nowhere else in the module. Dunder and decorated methods, private names defined twice, classes with bases from other modules (a base may call the private hook) and tests are not reported. Subclasses in other modules that override the private method are not analyzed. Repair: Move the private method's body and async/def kind into the public method, keep the public name, signature and docstring, and delete the private method. Keep the split with a reasoned suppression when a subclass overrides the private method. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/redundant-private-delegate: hint}, or select VIS006.
^VIS006$.markdownDescription:
**VIS006 — visibility/redundant-private-delegate**

A method only forwards its parameters to a private method used nowhere else.

def events(self, *, run_id): return self._events(run_id=run_id) adds a second name and a jump without behavior: calling an async generator already defers its body until iteration, so moving the body into events behaves the same. Validation before the call is the legitimate reason for the split, so only a body consisting of one return is reported. The private method must be an undecorated method of the same class with the same parameter names and kinds, receive every parameter unchanged, and be referenced nowhere else in the module. Dunder and decorated methods, private names defined twice, classes with bases from other modules (a base may call the private hook) and tests are not reported. Subclasses in other modules that override the private method are not analyzed.

**Problem**
```python
class Frames:
    def events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        return self._events(run_id=run_id)

    async def _events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        async for frame in self._source(run_id):
            yield frame
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Frames:
    async def events(self, *, run_id: UUID) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame]:
        async for frame in self._source(run_id):
            yield frame
```

Move the private method's body and async/def kind into the public method, keep the public name, signature and docstring, and delete the private method. Keep the split with a reasoned suppression when a subclass overrides the private method. No automatic rewrite is performed. ^VIS007$.description: A module contains more private definitions than the configured limit. A growing collection of private models and helpers can make a module's responsibility harder to understand. Private uppercase assignments with values are listed separately as constants and never contribute to the limit. Imports, ordinary assignment-style type aliases, methods, nested/local definitions and definitions inside control-flow statements are excluded. Package initializers are checked too. A few models beside their consumer remain valid at the default limit of 12. Even a larger cohesive model tree or parser may be intentional: this metric does not infer cohesion, separable groups or safe extraction. Choose a name describing that responsibility; models.py is only one possibility. Preserve import direction, initialization, framework registration and module visibility when moving code. ^VIS008$.title: VIS008: A package initializer spells a re-export against its configured convention.
^VIS008$.description: A package initializer spells a re-export against its configured convention. Use style.reexports to give package APIs a consistent spelling. all reports explicit same-name import aliases and uses __all__ for the public export list. alias reports ordinary imports named by a statically resolved __all__ when a same-name alias can mark the re-export. Existing aliases can coexist with an intentional runtime export list. The rule considers unique, direct import bindings in production __init__.py files. Real renames, dotted module imports, guarded or rebound names and star imports are outside its inference. Selecting the rule without a style uses all. Repair: With all, use a plain import and include the name in __all__ if it belongs to the public API. With alias, use a same-name alias such as Event as Event and preserve an intentional runtime export list. For a package that needs either spelling, set reexports to allow in a style override with a reason. This is a read-only check.

Use style.reexports to give package APIs a consistent spelling. all reports explicit same-name import aliases and uses __all__ for the public export list. alias reports ordinary imports named by a statically resolved __all__ when a same-name alias can mark the re-export. Existing aliases can coexist with an intentional runtime export list. The rule considers unique, direct import bindings in production __init__.py files. Real renames, dotted module imports, guarded or rebound names and star imports are outside its inference. Selecting the rule without a style uses all.

**Problem**


**Preferred**

^VIS009$.title: VIS009: A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module.
^VIS009$.description: A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), packages outside source selection and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent. Findings expose the configured usage_scope. When no references exist inside the defining module either, the finding says unused outside tests among analyzed modules and lists the internal reference evidence. Prefer testing the public behavior that calls it. If direct helper tests are deliberate, keep a reasoned private-access exception; if it is a supported external API, declare it in __all__ or document a reasoned suppression. Review callers before renaming.

architecture/layer-boundary.title: ARC001: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
architecture/layer-boundary.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.import_graph.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

**Preferred**

architecture/cross-feature-import.title: ARC002: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
architecture/cross-feature-import.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

architecture/forbidden-third-party-impor.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. architecture/import-cycle.title: ARC004: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.
architecture/import-cycle.description: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (ARC001, ARC002, ARC006) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

Defaults and existing finding identities are retained.

```python
# voice/application/calls.py

```

**Preferred**

```python
# billing/application/invoices.py subscribes to it.
```

architecture/missing-facade-export.title: ARC008: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.
architecture/missing-facade-export.description: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export. A contract's min_importers_to_export threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional architecture.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before. Repair: Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. architecture/member-boundary.title: ARC009: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist.
architecture/member-boundary.description: A workspace member imports a member outside its may_depend_on allowlist. Member-local layers describe internal design; workspace member boundaries describe which projects may depend on one another. Only direct production imports between discovered members count. Unmatched source members are unrestricted, overlapping source globs combine their allowances, and imports inside one member always pass. Wiring and shared modules retain these boundaries. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply. Repair: Move the dependency to an allowed member or invert it behind an interface; change the root allowlist only if the dependency belongs in the intended design.

TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking; transitive does not apply.

**Problem**


**Preferred**

architecture/undeclared-member-dependenc.title: ARC010: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency.
architecture/undeclared-member-dependenc.description: A workspace member imports another member without declaring a direct project dependency. One shared import graph makes undeclared imports work locally, but the member may fail when installed independently. This rule compares direct production imports with project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and tool.uv.sources. Distribution names are normalized independently of Python package names. Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations. Repair: For an allowed dependency, declare the imported member's distribution in project.dependencies and configure its uv workspace source. If architecture.members forbids the dependency, remove the import or move the dependency behind an allowed member boundary.

Markers and extras count without evaluating the analyzer's environment. uv sources alone do not declare dependencies. A member source overrides the root source, even when marked. Dependency groups and test imports are not assessed; projects with dynamic dependencies or without static metadata are skipped. architecture.import_graph.transitive does not require transitive declarations.

**Problem**

```toml
name = "api"
dependencies = []
# api imports core.model
```

**Preferred**

architecture/missing-required-module.title: ARC014: A package is missing a required module or public entry point.

Do not add empty implementation stubs solely to satisfy the check.

complexity/excess-attribute-depth.title: CPX001: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes.
complexity/excess-attribute-depth.description: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes. An instance method that reaches through several stored collaborators depends on their internal arrangement. This opt-in Law of Demeter review reports calls with at least two consecutive attribute accesses from the instance receiver before the first method call, such as self.browser.input.motor(). One finding covers a whole receiver call chain. Direct collaborator calls, pure data reads and fluent chains starting from a direct collaborator are excluded. Module objects stored from unshadowed imports or declared as ModuleType, explicit SimpleNamespace trees, and typed dataclass/Pydantic record paths ending in known containers or values are namespaces rather than collaborator graphs. Known pathlib parent paths and subprocess pipes also retain their standard APIs. Namespace evidence comes from annotations, direct constructor assignments and property return annotations; analyzed imports and re-exports are followed without executing code. Every intermediate object must be a known namespace or value: a record containing a service does not exempt navigation into that service. Names such as api, client, get or append alone exempt nothing. Unknown SDK types and dynamic property/data flow remain review limitations. Decorated and implicit class/static methods, nested helper bodies, comprehensions, receiver rebinding and navigation through parameters, aliases or subscripts are outside the review. This is a bounded review, not proof of a design defect. When namespace evidence is incomplete, the finding includes the declared/constructed root type and the unresolved step. These are review inputs for an agent, not proof that the API is poorly designed. Inspect the public API contract before choosing a refactor; an intentional namespace can be a valid conclusion. Repair: Review whether the caller should receive the needed collaborator directly or ask its direct collaborator to perform the operation. A local variable alone does not reduce structural coupling. Preserve factory/property evaluation and object lifetimes; repeated lookups need not return the same object. Keep intentional API navigation with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned CPX001 suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable with rules: {complexity/excess-attribute-depth: hint}, globally or in a package override, or --select CPX001.

complexity/inline-call-argument.title: CPX002: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.
complexity/inline-call-argument.description: An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument. Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded. Repair: Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.
complexity/inline-call-argument.markdownDescription:
**CPX002 — complexity/inline-call-argument**

An awaited result, eager comprehension or builtin reduction is passed directly as a call argument.

Naming an intermediate value before passing it on separates the suspension point or collection transformation from the construction or call that consumes it, and gives the value a name in tracebacks and debuggers. This opt-in syntax review reports a direct positional or named keyword argument of a call in production code that is one of the kinds in call_argument_kinds (all by default): await (an await expression, including nested forms such as await f(await g())), comprehension (a list, set or dict comprehension, even when CPX006 accepts its internal logic) or aggregate (an unshadowed builtin all, any, max, min, sorted or sum reducing a generator expression; the whole reduction is named and the generator stays lazy). It applies to any call without inferring constructors or runtime types and reports each argument once. Plain awaits, return await, named values, other calls and attribute reads, generator expressions passed directly, starred arguments and values nested inside another argument expression are outside scope. Arguments within lambdas, comprehensions, conditional expressions, boolean operators, while conditions, chained comparisons and assert messages are skipped because extraction would change when or how often they run. Tests are excluded.

**Problem**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    return Response(
        text=await browser.clipboard.read(),
        users=[to_user(user) for user in result.users],
        active=sum(user.active for user in result.users),
    )
```

**Preferred**
```python
async def to_response(browser, result):
    text = await browser.clipboard.read()
    users = [to_user(user) for user in result.users]
    active = sum(user.active for user in result.users)
    return Response(text=text, users=users, active=active)
```

Assign the value to a local variable in the statement before the call and pass that variable; a named keyword supplies a suggested variable name. Preserve the callable lookup, argument evaluation order, guards and suspension points: moving an argument before the call can evaluate it before earlier arguments or the callable itself. Do not eagerly materialize generator expressions. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/inline-call-argument: hint}, select CPX002, or set call_argument_kinds under style or in a style override, which also narrows the review to that scope. Reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain complexity/inline-call-argument` for details.

complexity/excess-positional-parameters.title: CPX003: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows.
complexity/excess-positional-parameters.description: A function accepts more positional parameters than its package allows. Call sites such as connect(user, run, tab, True) do not say which value is which, and swapping two arguments of the same type still type-checks. The max of the rule entry is the limit (5 when omitted); parameters after that limit must be keyword-only so every call names them. self and cls are not counted, nor are *args and **kwargs. Dunder methods, @overload and @override definitions are exempt because their signatures are dictated elsewhere, and tests are not checked. Positional-only parameters count like any other positional parameter. Repair: Insert * after the last allowed positional parameter, then pass the remaining arguments by keyword at every call site. Callbacks whose positional signature is fixed by a framework keep it with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {complexity/excess-positional-parameters: {severity: warning, max: 3}}; an entry in a style override's rules refines the limit for that package.
complexity/excess-positional-parameters.markdownDescription:
**CPX003 — complexity/excess-positional-parameters**

The max of the rule entry is the limit (5 when omitted); parameters after that limit must be keyword-only so every call names them. self and cls are not counted, nor are *args and **kwargs. Dunder methods, @overload and @override definitions are exempt because their signatures are dictated elsewhere, and tests are not checked. Positional-only parameters count like any other positional parameter.

**Problem**
