complexity/duplicate-function.title: CPX004: A module-level function repeats another function's code.
complexity/duplicate-function.description: A module-level function repeats another function's code. Copy-pasted helpers drift: a fix or a changed message lands in one copy and the others keep the old behavior, and readers cannot tell whether the difference is intended. This opt-in review compares module-level functions within each analyzed root package and reports every function whose parameters, annotations, decorators and body are identical to another one's, ignoring names, docstrings, comments and formatting. A body needs at least three statements, counting nested ones, so trivial one-liners are not reported. Methods, nested functions, test files and separate root packages are not compared. Each copy gets its own finding with the other locations. Repair: Keep one copy in a module both callers may import, usually in their nearest common package, and import it from there. Check architecture boundaries and import cycles when choosing the owner. Copies that must evolve independently keep a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/duplicate-function: warning}, or select CPX004.

complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.title: CPX005: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.
complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.description: A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional. Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used. Repair: Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.
complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional.markdownDescription:
**CPX005 — complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional**

A conditional expression directly contains another result conditional.

Nested conditional expressions hide a multi-branch decision inside one expression. This opt-in style review reports a conditional whose body or else branch is another conditional expression, once at the outermost expression in each directly connected chain. Conditionals inside tests, calls, lambdas or comprehensions are separate expressions; their presence alone does not make the enclosing conditional nested. Simple fallbacks and independent conditionals remain valid. Only production source is checked; no type or runtime inference is used.

**Problem**
```python
status = OK if completed else TIMEOUT if timed_out else ERROR
```

**Preferred**
```python
if completed:
    status = OK
elif timed_out:
    status = TIMEOUT
else:
    status = ERROR
```

Use explicit if/elif or match statements. Preserve branch order, precedence and lazy evaluation; an eagerly evaluated dictionary can change behavior. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional: hint}, or select CPX005. Package overrides and reasoned suppressions are supported.

Run `smelt explain complexity/forbidden-nested-conditional` for details.

complexity/excess-comprehension-loops.title: CPX006: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps.
complexity/excess-comprehension-loops.description: A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps. This opt-in syntax review reports comprehensions with too many for clauses, a conditional element/value with a nontrivial branch, or multiple filters (including a boolean filter with more than two operands). Names, attribute reads and constants are trivial branches. Nested comprehension triggers are grouped at the outermost comprehension. Simple mapping, a single filter and trivial fallbacks remain valid. Only production source is checked; no types or runtime costs are inferred. Repair: Name the per-item decision or use an explicit loop. Preserve generator laziness, iteration/filter order and conditional evaluation. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/excess-comprehension-loops: hint} or select CPX006; set max on the entry, e.g. {severity: hint, max: 2}. The limit defaults to 1; an entry in a style override's rules can permit intentional flattening.
complexity/excess-comprehension-loops.markdownDescription:
**CPX006 — complexity/excess-comprehension-loops**

A comprehension combines too many iteration or decision steps.

This opt-in syntax review reports comprehensions with too many for clauses, a conditional element/value with a nontrivial branch, or multiple filters (including a boolean filter with more than two operands). Names, attribute reads and constants are trivial branches. Nested comprehension triggers are grouped at the outermost comprehension. Simple mapping, a single filter and trivial fallbacks remain valid. Only production source is checked; no types or runtime costs are inferred.

**Problem**
```python
values = [convert(x) if x.ready else fallback(x) for x in items]
```

**Preferred**
```python
values = [resolve_item(x) for x in items]
```

complexity/excess-constructor-decisions.title: CPX007: A constructor contains more decisions than the configured limit.
complexity/excess-constructor-decisions.description: A constructor contains more decisions than the configured limit. Normalization, validation and derivation become easier to understand when named separately from object initialization. Do not extract arbitrary fragments merely to lower a count. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {complexity/excess-constructor-decisions: hint} or select CPX007; set max on the entry, in the root or a style override's rules. The limit defaults to 2; 0 forbids any counted decision. idioms/bundled-instance-assignment.title: IDM001: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.
idioms/bundled-instance-assignment.description: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention. Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error. Repair: Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. Parallel assignments, swaps, descriptors and unpacking failures can behave differently when split, so there is no automatic rewrite.

idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch.title: IDM002: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.
idioms/prefer-match-type-dispatch.description: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy. Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior. Repair: Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.

idioms/prefer-callable-instance.title: IDM003: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method.
idioms/prefer-callable-instance.description: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method. A class with one public instance method can express its operation through __call__ and a class name describing that operation. This opt-in design review reports one candidate per plain class with exactly one directly declared public method. Private helpers and __init__ do not count as public operations. An existing __call__ is already a callable API and is never reported. Constructor and operation signatures are reported separately, including positional-only, keyword-only and variadic arguments: construction configures the object, while __call__ must retain the method's call-time arguments and async behavior. Classes with bases, metaclass keywords, class or method decorators, additional special methods, class-level data or conditional definitions are excluded. This keeps inherited APIs, descriptors, dataclasses and explicit protocols outside this bounded syntax review. Test files are excluded. A single method does not prove a design defect: published named APIs and stateful lifecycles can justify keeping the class as it is. Dynamic monkey-patching and external API consumers are not resolved. Repair: Consider renaming the sole public method to __call__ and naming the class after its operation (for example, ReportService.generate becomes GenerateReport.__call__). Preserve the constructor signature, call-time parameters, defaults, return annotations and async behavior; do not move constructor dependencies into __call__. Review callers, dependency injection registrations and public compatibility before changing either name. No names, arguments or callers are rewritten automatically. Enable rules: {idioms/prefer-callable-instance: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select IDM003. Keep an intentional named API with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned IDM003 suppression.

idioms/redundant-name-alias.title: IDM004: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name.
idioms/redundant-name-alias.description: A module-level name only repeats another class or function name. Two names for one class or function make readers and agents ask whether they differ, and grep finds only half of the uses. Such aliases are typically compatibility names left behind by a rename or placeholders for a union that never gained a second member. This opt-in review reports unconditional module-level X = Y, X: TypeAlias = Y and type X = Y statements whose right side is a bare name or dotted attribute that refers to a class or function defined in the same module, or to an imported CapWords name. Type expressions such as unions, subscripts and Annotated, values such as constants, conditional assignments (version or import fallbacks), class-level names, typing special forms such as Any and tests are not reported. Repair: Use the target name everywhere and remove the alias. Introduce a shared name once it describes a real type expression, such as a union with a second member. Keep a deliberate public compatibility name with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/redundant-name-alias: hint}, or select IDM004.

idioms/missing-interface-docstring.title: IDM005: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring.
idioms/missing-interface-docstring.description: An abstract or Protocol method has a placeholder body and no docstring. A port or interface method has no implementation to read, so its docstring is the only place that states the contract: what the method guarantees, what it requires and what it leaves untouched. A bare ... body leaves implementers and callers to guess, and one undocumented member next to documented siblings usually means the contract was forgotten, not that it is obvious. This opt-in review reports @abstractmethod methods (including abstract properties) and methods of typing.Protocol classes whose body is only ..., pass or raise NotImplementedError and which have no docstring. Methods with a default implementation, @overload/@override signatures, property setters/deleters, dunder methods other than __call__ and tests are not reported. Ordinary Protocol attributes have no body and are out of scope. Repair: Replace the placeholder body with a docstring that states the method's contract; a docstring alone is a valid body, so drop the ... (Ruff PIE790 reports a placeholder left after a docstring). No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-interface-docstring: hint}, or select IDM005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

idioms/missing-broad-except-reason.title: IDM006: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything.
idioms/missing-broad-except-reason.description: A broad exception handler does not say why it catches everything. Catching Exception, BaseException or everything with a bare except is sometimes the right call: a background task must survive a failing callback, or a best-effort lookup may fail in many ways. Which of these applies is invisible in the code itself, and a linter pragma such as '# noqa: BLE001' or '# pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught' records only that the warning was silenced, not why. Without the reason, a reviewer cannot tell a deliberate boundary from a swallowed bug. This opt-in review reports an except clause whose type is Exception, BaseException, a tuple containing one of them, or missing, when no explanatory comment sits on the except line, on the comment lines directly above it, or between the except line and the first statement of its body, including a trailing comment on that statement. Tool directives such as noqa, pylint: disable, type: ignore, pragma: no cover and smelt: ignore do not count as an explanation, but text after them does. Handlers whose last statement is a raise and that contain no return, break or continue always propagate the failure and are not reported. Tests are not reported. Repair: Catch the specific exceptions the code can recover from. When the handler must stay broad, add a comment that states why, for example which boundary it protects or why any failure is acceptable. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/missing-broad-except-reason: hint}, or select IDM006. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert.title: IDM007: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute.
idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert.description: Several methods of a class assert the same narrowing of a self attribute. assert self._stack is not None in one method narrows a type for the checker. When several methods of the class repeat it, the attribute is optional in its type but required after setup, and every caller depends on a check that python -O removes. This opt-in review reports, once per class and expression, an assert of self.<attribute> is not None or isinstance(self.<attribute>, ...) that appears in at least two methods of the same class, including each operand of an and. Asserts in nested functions belong to that function, static methods are skipped and tests are not checked. Unlike a blanket assert ban, single local narrowings stay valid. Repair: Make the attribute required by constructing it before the object is used, or read it through one property or accessor that raises an error naming the missing setup step. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {idioms/duplicate-narrowing-assert: warning}, or select IDM007.

idioms/loop-invariant-collection.title: IDM008: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs.
idioms/loop-invariant-collection.description: A membership lookup set is rebuilt in a loop from stable immutable inputs. Repeated lookup-set construction can turn one validation pass into quadratic work and obscure a shared domain set. This opt-in review requires positive, file-local evidence: homogeneous immutable tuple literals, tuple[T, ...] annotations, or tuple fields of standard-library frozen dataclasses declared in the same module. Scalar projections may read directly declared fields of those frozen records. Annotations are assumed to describe standard builtin values and these concrete record types; runtime subclass overrides or frozen-state bypasses are not proved safe. This is not a runtime immutability proof. Records with bases, extra decorators or custom attribute access are excluded, as are descriptors, unknown fields and imported record types. Minimum snapshot evidence is a local @dataclass(frozen=True) record with a plain id: str field and a tuple[Record, ...] input; the outer iteration must also be a known tuple. The original Harnessed example uses Pydantic dataclasses and Annotated fields, which this initial implementation deliberately does not infer. Only direct for loops with a simple name target in functions or ordinary methods are reviewed; while and async loops are not inferred. The body must consist of passive scalar/tuple expressions, simple local assignments, conditionals, returns, breaks/continues or literal builtin error raises. Unknown calls, mutation through aliases, properties, nested loops/scopes, await/yield and uncertain operations make it stay quiet. A single-generator set comprehension must produce known builtin scalar values and appear on the right of in/not in. Equivalent projections are grouped per loop, including renamed comprehension variables. Tests are ignored. Repair: Review computing the lookup set once and reusing it. Preserve the empty-loop case, guards, exception timing and evaluation order: moving construction before a loop or guard can evaluate code that previously never ran. Keep lazy initialization at the first required check when necessary. No automatic hoisting is provided. Enable rules: {idioms/loop-invariant-collection: hint}, or select IDM008.

imports/excess-package-imports.title: IMP001: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.
imports/excess-package-imports.description: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, including its facade when mixed with implementation imports, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Findings include missing static exports and a cycle witness for the proposed caller/facade edges. Known cycles block bundling advice. No-cycle-found covers only explicit runtime imports; dynamic imports and implicit package initialization remain unproven. Discovered tests and conftest.py also count as outside callers, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. This does not change ARC008's separate count_tests opt-in for API expansion. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Use proposed_exports to review missing re-exports. A cycle_check of cycle blocks bundling: keep the imports or resolve dependency direction first. No automatic rewrite is performed. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.

imports/excess-module-imports.title: IMP002: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows.
imports/excess-module-imports.description: A module imports more project modules than its policy allows. Many independent project dependencies can signal that a module coordinates too many responsibilities. Unlike IMP001, this review counts distinct direct target modules across every project root package, without requiring a contract on each target package. Repeated imports and multiple symbols from one module count once. Facade re-exports count at the facade path used by the caller, not at their defining modules. Standard-library and third-party imports never count; TYPE_CHECKING imports follow the existing architecture.import_graph.type_checking policy. Initializers and declared composition roots are exempt by default. This is a design hint, not proof of excessive coupling; reducing imports alone does not simplify a design. Repair: Split a cohesive responsibility into its own module or depend on deliberate package facades. Review import cycles and initializer side effects before adding re-exports. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {imports/excess-module-imports: {severity: hint, max: 15}}; max defaults to 20, zero is supported, and an entry in a style override's rules refines it for that package. module_import_exemptions defaults to [facades, composition_root]; [] checks both.

Many independent project dependencies can signal that a module coordinates too many responsibilities. Unlike IMP001, this review counts distinct direct target modules across every project root package, without requiring a contract on each target package. Repeated imports and multiple symbols from one module count once. Facade re-exports count at the facade path used by the caller, not at their defining modules. Standard-library and third-party imports never count; TYPE_CHECKING imports follow the existing architecture.import_graph.type_checking policy. Initializers and declared composition roots are exempt by default. This is a design hint, not proof of excessive coupling; reducing imports alone does not simplify a design.

**Problem**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.users.read import Read
from app.users.write import Write
from app.billing.pay import Pay
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/client.py, after deliberate facade review
from app.users import Read, Write
from app.billing import Pay
```

Split a cohesive responsibility into its own module or depend on deliberate package facades. Review import cycles and initializer side effects before adding re-exports. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it with rules: {imports/excess-module-imports: {severity: hint, max: 15}}; max defaults to 20, zero is supported, and an entry in a style override's rules refines it for that package. module_import_exemptions defaults to [facades, composition_root]; [] checks both.

Run `smelt explain imports/excess-module-imports` for details.

With relative style and max_relative_level: 1, local imports use one dot; parent and cross-root imports stay absolute. Deeper relative imports can be explicitly allowed. The closest style override supplies the style, else style.imports. No style is enforced without one, and this rule never changes bindings. Repair: Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. There is no automatic rewrite.

imports/prefer-package-import.title: IMP004: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import.
imports/prefer-package-import.description: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import. Importing supported names from a common package keeps callers independent of implementation paths and allows related imports to be combined. This opt-in hint requires every name in a from-import to have an unconditional, direct, same-named public re-export in an analyzed ancestor __init__.py. The nearest eligible package is suggested. Static __all__ is respected. Production imports inside that package are excluded to avoid routing its own implementation through its initializer. Discovered tests and conftest.py are checked, including configured test roots inside the package. Test-quality exclusions do not exempt imports; project exclusions and normal suppressions apply. Imports in package initializers also stay unchanged. Conditional, rebound, private, star and dynamic exports, re-export chains, module imports and unscanned third-party packages are outside this check. Repair: Use the suggested package import and combine it with an existing import there when both are in the same scope and guard. Preserve aliases, comments and relative/absolute import policy. Review initializer side effects and dependency cycles. No exports are created and no automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

layout/module-docstring-convention.description: A module docstring is missing or present against the package's module_docstrings convention. layout/definition-order.title: LAY004: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries.
layout/definition-order.description: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries. Public interfaces should be easy to find. A stable topological order prioritizes configured categories while preserving category order, definition-time reads, rebinding and execution barriers. Function bodies are deferred; decorators, defaults, assignments and eager annotations are not. Future imports and declared Python 3.14+ targets defer annotations. Unions of recognized, unshadowed builtin types (and None) are modeled in eager function annotations for declared Python 3.10+ targets; imported or user-defined types and operator expressions in defaults remain unknown. Overload/property families remain atomic. Unknown execution is pinned. Attribute dictionaries of unambiguous undecorated nested functions are distinct from the enclosing ordered namespace, so vars(local_function) and local_function.__dict__ alone do not block enclosing moves. Nonlocal closure writes alone are also unrelated to module/class definition order. Unknown receivers, globals, locals, vars(), global writes and code/annotation introspection still require review. Repair: Review the expected order and execution barriers. Explicit check --fix can apply bounded moves where the package permits safe-only fixes. Imports, unknown execution and a misplaced main guard require manual review. Names and visibility are never rewritten by ordering. Refused sections identify the triggering expression and its source location in fix_blocker and fix_reason; the safety boundary stays in place. Pinned definitions are listed under coverage.ordering[].barriers with check --format json --show-coverage. Dependencies take precedence over public-first order. On Python 3.12/3.13, keep a needed annotations future import when the chosen order uses forward references; TYP002 retains it.

layout/misplaced-static-helper.title: LAY005: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function.
layout/misplaced-static-helper.description: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function. A helper that needs neither instance nor class state is often easier to find and reuse as a private module function. This package convention reviews direct sync/async methods carrying only the recognized builtin staticmethod decorator, including import aliases. Known or unresolved external same-named attribute access preserves static APIs. Classes with inheritance, subclasses or decorators, additional method decorators, special methods, __class__/super references and detected class-namespace dependencies are excluded. This is a placement preference, not proof of equivalent runtime behavior; external/dynamic consumers and definition-time dependencies still need review. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Repair: Move the helper to module scope with a leading underscore, remove @staticmethod, and update class/instance-qualified calls and callback references. Preserve annotations, defaults, evaluation order and dependencies; choose a distinct name if the module already binds it. Keep deliberate static APIs with a closest package rule set to off or reasoned suppression. No automatic extraction is performed.

layout/callee-before-caller.title: LAY006: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls.
layout/callee-before-caller.description: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls. A step-down reading order introduces a higher-level operation before its lower-level helpers. This opt-in review covers stable undecorated top-level sync/async functions and direct methods on undecorated classes without bases. It resolves direct same-module names and receiver.method calls, excludes shadowed bindings, nested scopes, comprehensions, dunder methods and recursive call components, and respects definition-time parameter/return dependencies. Only same-visibility pairs are reviewed so LAY004's public-first categories retain precedence. Dynamic lookup, inherited APIs and general call graphs are not inferred. This is a reading convention, not a correctness check. Repair: Review placing the caller before its helper within the same public/private group. Preserve defaults, decorators, annotations, rebinding and execution barriers. No definitions are reordered automatically; LAY004 independently handles public-first ordering and its bounded fixer. Enable rules: {layout/callee-before-caller: hint} or select LAY006; package overrides and reasoned suppressions apply.

layout/misplaced-private-constant.title: LAY008: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module.
layout/misplaced-private-constant.description: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module. Implementation constants such as a controller's supported file extensions belong beside the class as private module constants when they do not form part of its object contract. This opt-in convention reports private UPPER_CASE names assigned literal scalars or recursively literal sets, lists, tuples and dictionaries in production class bodies, including annotated, chained and guarded assignments. It checks nested and local classes independently. Classes with bases, decorators or class keywords are excluded conservatively because inheritance, enums, data models and metaclasses can give attributes a class-specific contract. Public names, lowercase fields, dunder names, instance assignments, method locals, calls, comprehensions and values referring to other names are outside scope. This is a placement convention; syntax alone cannot prove that callers never override or mutate an attribute. Repair: Move the constant to the same module with a leading underscore, then update class-qualified and instance-qualified reads to use the constant name directly. Check name collisions, initialization order, name mangling, mutation, subclass overrides and external consumers before moving it. Keep intentional class contracts with a reasoned suppression or package override. Enable rules: {layout/misplaced-private-constant: error} to block the convention, or --select LAY008 to review it. No automatic move or rewrite is performed.

layout/redundant-module-name.title: LAY009: A module filename repeats context already supplied by an ancestor package.
layout/redundant-module-name.description: A module filename repeats context already supplied by an ancestor package. cars.application.car_exporter repeats the cars context; cars.application.exporter keeps the responsibility visible without restating the path. This opt-in review checks a whole ancestor package name at either underscore-delimited end of a module name, including across intervening layer packages. It also recognizes a single regular trailing s (cars/car, purchase_orders/purchase_order). It does not infer irregular plurals or strip ss, us, is, ies, ses, xes, zes, ches or shes endings. Leading underscores are preserved. Substrings, names with no remaining responsibility, package names, dunder modules and separately discovered tests are outside scope. Source-root directory names are not package context. Findings are advisory because repetition may serve a published API or domain meaning. Repair: Review the shorter filename and update imports and facade exports when renaming. An occupied module/package name is not suggested. No files are renamed automatically. Enable with rules: {layout/redundant-module-name: hint}, globally or in a style override, or --select LAY009. Use a package off override or a reasoned file suppression for intentional public names.

modeling/redundant-str-enum-value.title: MOD001: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member.
modeling/redundant-str-enum-value.description: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member. StrEnum members are already strings, so extracting .value often adds noise and loses the enum type unnecessarily. This opt-in hint recognizes direct Class.MEMBER.value reads on analyzed, top-level classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum, including import aliases, relative imports and analyzed re-exports. Simple string, auto() and member-alias declarations are supported. Ordinary Enum, str/Enum mixins, unknown or shadowed bindings, custom enum construction/value access, instance variables and dynamic lookups are excluded. Shadowing anywhere in a module conservatively limits recognition there. Repair: Prefer the member directly when the consumer accepts string subclasses. Review boundary behavior first: exact str checks, identity, repr and serialization contracts can distinguish the member from its raw value. Literal-typed parameters can also reject the member in a type checker; Smelt has no consumer type information. Keep .value or an explicit str(member) conversion where a plain string is intentional, and suppress the hint with a reason. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix.title: MOD002: A class definition carries a Base prefix or suffix instead of a responsibility.
modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix.description: A class definition carries a Base prefix or suffix instead of a responsibility. BaseService and MessageBase name a position in an inheritance hierarchy rather than the abstraction's responsibility. A responsibility-based name such as Service keeps that implementation choice out of the name. The affix does not itself create dependency coupling, and inheritance can be intentional, so this is an opt-in naming convention rather than a correctness check or an inheritance ban. It checks all class definitions in production modules, including private, nested and local classes, without inferring whether they have subclasses. After leading underscores, a prefix Base must be the whole name or be followed by an uppercase letter or underscore; a suffix Base must follow a non-empty name. Baseline, Baseball, Database and Base64 remain valid. Imports, aliases, base-class expressions, function names and test files are outside scope; inheriting from an imported BaseModel is allowed. Repair: Choose a name describing the class's responsibility or contract, then update references and deliberate exports. Preserve inheritance where it serves the design. A more specific package rule can disable the convention for compatibility, or a reasoned suppression can preserve a published name. No symbols are renamed automatically. Enable with rules: {modeling/forbidden-base-class-affix: error}, globally or in a style override, or --select MOD002.

modeling/prefer-str-enum-discriminator.title: MOD003: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields.
modeling/prefer-str-enum-discriminator.description: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields. Discriminated union variants often repeat protocol strings in Literal annotations, field defaults and dispatch code. A shared StrEnum gives those values one named definition while Literal[EventType.MEMBER] preserves each variant's narrow type. This opt-in syntax review recognizes directly annotated class fields named type, kind or tag whose typing.Literal contains exactly one raw string, with or without a default. It supports typing and typing_extensions import aliases, quoted annotations and Annotated/Required/NotRequired wrappers. Dataclasses, model classes and class-based TypedDict declarations use the same syntax. The field shape is a review candidate, not proof of union membership. Other field names, multiple-value Literals, enum-member Literals, ClassVar, type aliases, inherited fields and uncertain or shadowed typing bindings are excluded. Declared Python minima before 3.11 are excluded; unknown minima require version review. Repair: Define or reuse a shared StrEnum for the union's wire values. Keep each variant annotated as Literal[EnumType.MEMBER], and use that same member in direct defaults, dataclasses.field(default=...) or model Field(default=...). Keep explicit string values such as checkpoint.extension; auto() may change the wire contract. Review consumers and serialization before changing defaults, since exact str checks and repr can distinguish enum members. StrEnum requires Python 3.11+. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed. Suppress intentional external schema strings with a reason or disable this review for their package.

**Problem**
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal

@dataclass
class CheckpointExtension:
    tag: str
    data: dict[str, object]
    type: Literal["checkpoint.extension"] = field(default="checkpoint.extension", kw_only=True)
```

**Preferred**
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Literal

class EventType(StrEnum):
    CHECKPOINT_EXTENSION = "checkpoint.extension"

@dataclass
class CheckpointExtension:
    tag: str
    data: dict[str, object]
    type: Literal[EventType.CHECKPOINT_EXTENSION] = field(default=EventType.CHECKPOINT_EXTENSION, kw_only=True)
```

Keep each variant annotated as Literal[EnumType.MEMBER], and use that same member in direct defaults, dataclasses.field(default=...) or model Field(default=...). Keep explicit string values such as checkpoint.extension; auto() may change the wire contract. Review consumers and serialization before changing defaults, since exact str checks and repr can distinguish enum members. StrEnum requires Python 3.11+. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed. Suppress intentional external schema strings with a reason or disable this review for their package.

modeling/str-enum-value-convention.title: MOD004: A StrEnum spells its values against the configured auto/explicit convention.
modeling/str-enum-value-convention.description: A StrEnum spells its values against the configured auto/explicit convention. Under auto, a class with custom values such as 'mouseMoved' keeps explicit strings for every member and its auto() members are reported instead. It considers production classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum (imported as StrEnum, an alias or enum.StrEnum). Member aliases, private names and tests are ignored. Repair: Under explicit, spell each reported auto() member as its lowercased name, the value auto() produces for a StrEnum. Under auto, replace each reported explicit string with auto(), or spell the auto() members of a class with custom values explicitly. No automatic rewrite is performed. modeling/dataclass-field-mutation.title: MOD005: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction.
modeling/dataclass-field-mutation.description: A dataclass mutates its own fields after construction. A dataclass reads as a value: its generated __init__ is the constructor and its fields are what callers may rely on. When methods keep writing to self, the class is really a mutable accumulator or state machine with a value-like surface: callers can construct it in a half-built state, observe fields that are only scratch space for private helpers, and share instances whose contents change underneath them. Building the values first and passing them to a frozen dataclass, or keeping the accumulation in a plain class with private attributes, makes the lifecycle explicit. This opt-in review reports a @dataclass that is not frozen=True when a method other than __post_init__ assigns, deletes or augments an attribute of self, assigns or deletes an item of a field, calls a mutating container method such as append, add, update, pop or discard on a field declared as a mutable container, or calls setattr on self. Mutations inside nested functions of a method count. Calls that mutate through other objects, classes that are not dataclasses and tests are not reported. Intentional mutable records can keep a reasoned suppression. Repair: Compute the field values first and pass them to the constructor of a frozen dataclass, using immutable field types such as tuple, frozenset or Mapping; derive further values with properties or dataclasses.replace. When the object genuinely accumulates state, make it a plain class whose scratch attributes are private, or move the accumulation into a separate builder. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/dataclass-field-mutation: hint}, or select MOD005. Package overrides and reasoned inline suppressions are supported.

modeling/missing-dataclass-option.title: MOD006: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires.
modeling/missing-dataclass-option.description: A dataclass does not set an option its package requires. Whether a dataclass is frozen, uses slots or takes keyword-only arguments changes how callers may use it, yet codebases drift between @dataclass, @dataclass(frozen=True) and @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) without anyone being able to tell which deviations are deliberate. A style override lists dataclass_options, any of frozen, slots and kw_only, and every production @dataclass in the package must set each of them to True. An option that is missing or explicitly False is reported; a non-literal value is not judged. Missing slots is not reported when a base class comes from outside the project, such as a third-party or builtin class without __slots__, because slots save nothing there; bases from abc and typing still count. It is also not reported for classes with a functools.cached_property, which needs an instance __dict__. Nested packages can set their own list, and [] lifts the requirement. Tests are not checked. Repair: Add the missing options to the decorator. A dataclass that must stay mutable or unslotted keeps a reasoned suppression, or lives in a package whose contract sets its own dataclass_options. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {dataclass_options: [frozen, slots]}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

modeling/prefer-project-base-class.title: MOD007: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base.
modeling/prefer-project-base-class.description: A class inherits an outside base directly instead of the project base. Projects often wrap a framework base in their own base class to share configuration, for example a pydantic BaseModel subclass that sets extra='forbid' and frozen=True. A class that inherits the framework base directly silently misses that configuration, and nothing in the class tells a reviewer. A style override maps each outside base to the project base, e.g. bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}, and production classes in the package that list the outside base among their direct bases are reported. Bases are resolved through the module's imports, including aliases and module attributes. Only inheritance is judged: importing the outside base for annotations, isinstance checks or adapters stays valid. The module that defines the project base is exempt, a nested package can set bases: {} to allow direct inheritance, and single classes can keep a reasoned suppression. Tests are not checked. Repair: Inherit the project base named in the finding and drop configuration that only repeated it. When a class deliberately needs the outside base, keep a reasoned suppression or move it into a package whose contract sets bases: {}. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {bases: {pydantic.BaseModel: app.core.Options}}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

modeling/prefer-domain-exception.title: MOD008: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy.
modeling/prefer-domain-exception.description: Production code raises a builtin exception instead of the project hierarchy. A project exception hierarchy lets callers tell a domain failure apart from a programming error. Code that keeps raising ValueError or RuntimeError for domain failures, or converts every error into one, forces callers to catch broad builtins and guess what went wrong. A style override names the project base, e.g. errors: {base: app.errors.AppError}, and production code in the package that raises a builtin exception class, with or without arguments and with or without from, is reported. NotImplementedError, StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, GeneratorExit, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit are always allowed, and errors.allow adds more, e.g. [TypeError]. Bare re-raises, raising caught or project exceptions, names that shadow a builtin, raises in protocol dunder methods such as __getattr__ or __getitem__, and pydantic validators, which must raise ValueError or AssertionError, are not reported. Tests are not checked. Repair: Raise a subclass of the configured base that names the failure, and let callers catch that subclass. When callers rely on a builtin, for example TypeError for wrong argument types, add it to errors.allow, or set errors: {} in a nested package that deliberately raises builtins. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable it for the project with style: {errors: {base: app.errors.AppError}}, or for one package with the same option in a style override.

modeling/duplicate-class-name.title: MOD009: Two modules of one package define a public class with the same name.
modeling/duplicate-class-name.description: Two modules of one package define a public class with the same name. When two modules of the same package each define a public class called PageContent, imports, search results and review comments stop saying which one is meant, and the wrong import still type checks when the shapes are similar. This opt-in review groups public top-level classes by their nearest package, counting a package's __init__.py as part of that package, and reports every class whose name is also defined at the top level of another module there. Re-exports, private classes, nested classes, classes in separate packages and tests are not compared. Each definition gets its own finding with the other locations. Repair: Rename the classes after their role so each name says which one is meant, or merge them when they describe the same thing. A class that only exists as a private implementation detail can take a leading underscore. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/duplicate-class-name: warning}, or select MOD009.

modeling/implicit-duration-unit.title: MOD010: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number.
modeling/implicit-duration-unit.description: A numeric duration is named without its unit or written as an inline number. A constant called _FRAME_TIMEOUT = 2.0 does not say whether it means seconds or milliseconds, and asyncio.timeout(2.5) at two call sites drifts apart as soon as one of them is tuned. This opt-in review reports two forms. Names (kind constant, field or parameter): module constants, class fields and function parameters whose name ends in timeout, delay, interval, duration or wait and that hold a number: an int or float annotation, possibly wrapped in Final, ClassVar, Optional, Annotated or | None, or an unannotated int or float literal. Names that end in a unit, such as _TIMEOUT_SECONDS or quiet_ms, and values typed as timedelta are valid; @overload and @override signatures are not checked. Literals (kind literal): int and float literals passed as the duration of asyncio.timeout, asyncio.sleep, asyncio.wait_for, asyncio.wait, time.sleep and the anyio and trio sleep and timeout scopes, resolved through imports and aliases, and literals added to a clock reading such as loop.time() + 10 or time.monotonic() + 10. Ruff's PLR2004 only covers comparisons. sleep(0), which yields control instead of waiting, and tests are not checked. Repair: Append the unit to the name, e.g. _SECONDS or _ms, and convert once where the value enters the code, or type the value as datetime.timedelta. Move an inline duration into a module constant or configuration field whose name states its purpose and unit, and reuse it at every call site that means the same wait. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/implicit-duration-unit: warning}, or select MOD010.

modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.title: MOD011: A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field.
modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.description: A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field. frozen=True prevents rebinding fields, but list, dict and set contents can still change, including through a reference passed to the constructor. This opt-in ownership review reports each directly annotated built-in dict, list or set instance field on a dataclass explicitly decorated with frozen=True. It resolves module/import aliases and quoted annotations, conservatively skipping names bound again anywhere in the file, local imports and wildcard imports. ClassVar, InitVar, inherited fields, wrapped/union annotations, user-defined types and type aliases are outside its scope. Non-frozen classes and tests are ignored. A Mapping annotation is a read-only interface, not proof of runtime or deep immutability. Intentional mutable reference holders can keep a reasoned field suppression. Repair: Review ownership. Use tuple or frozenset for immutable sequences/sets. For a mapping, copy before wrapping it in MappingProxyType: wrapping the caller's original dict alone still reflects alias mutations. Changing only the annotation to Mapping freezes nothing. Copying or freezing may change behavior, so no automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass: warning}, or select MOD011.
modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-datacla.markdownDescription:
**MOD011 — modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass**

A frozen dataclass directly declares a mutable collection field.

frozen=True prevents rebinding fields, but list, dict and set contents can still change, including through a reference passed to the constructor. This opt-in ownership review reports each directly annotated built-in dict, list or set instance field on a dataclass explicitly decorated with frozen=True. It resolves module/import aliases and quoted annotations, conservatively skipping names bound again anywhere in the file, local imports and wildcard imports. ClassVar, InitVar, inherited fields, wrapped/union annotations, user-defined types and type aliases are outside its scope. Non-frozen classes and tests are ignored. A Mapping annotation is a read-only interface, not proof of runtime or deep immutability. Intentional mutable reference holders can keep a reasoned field suppression.

**Problem**
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arguments:
    names: dict[str, str]
```

**Preferred**
```python
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from types import MappingProxyType

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arguments:
    names: Mapping[str, str]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "names", MappingProxyType(dict(self.names)))
```

Review ownership. Use tuple or frozenset for immutable sequences/sets. For a mapping, copy before wrapping it in MappingProxyType: wrapping the caller's original dict alone still reflects alias mutations. Changing only the annotation to Mapping freezes nothing. Copying or freezing may change behavior, so no automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {modeling/mutable-field-in-frozen-dataclass: warning}, or select MOD011.

modeling/parallel-record-fields.title: MOD012: Stored sequence fields of one instance are paired by position.
modeling/parallel-record-fields.description: Stored sequence fields of one instance are paired by position. Parallel stored sequences leave their record relationship implicit: every constructor and transformation must preserve matching positions. zip(strict=True) checks lengths but cannot check the right pairing. This opt-in design review groups zip calls over at least two distinct sequence fields on the same instance, once per class and field group, with declaration and zip locations. It checks directly declared class annotations of list, tuple, Sequence and MutableSequence, including typing spellings, quoted annotations and module/import aliases. Preceding unconditional local aliases assigned once from a receiver field are supported. Only undecorated instance methods are inspected. Rebound names, starred arguments, inherited/untyped fields, ClassVar, nested functions and unknown types are skipped. Local sequences and different receivers remain valid. Tests are ignored. The rule cannot establish that the fields form a domain record: intentional column-oriented or numerical storage is valid and can use a reasoned suppression at the reported zip site. Repair: Review whether these fields model one logical record. If so, store one sequence of named records and update construction and consumers together. Preserve length validation and iteration order. Deliberate column storage may retain a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite or correctness claim is made. Enable rules: {modeling/parallel-record-fields: hint}, or select MOD012.

typing/forbidden-future-annotations.title: TYP001: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.
typing/forbidden-future-annotations.description: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy. An explicit source convention can forbid this import. In when-needed mode, a declared Python 3.14+ minimum also makes it a violation because annotations are already deferred by default. The future import still changes runtime representation, so removal requires checking annotation consumers and never happens automatically. Repair: Follow the declared convention while preserving forward references and runtime behavior. When-needed mode gives review hints on earlier or unknown targets and rejects the import on declared Python 3.14+ targets. An explicit allow exception can retain a runtime compatibility contract. No automatic rewrite is performed.

typing/redundant-future-annotations.title: TYP002: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need.
typing/redundant-future-annotations.description: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need. On targets before Python 3.14 or with an unknown minimum, when-needed mode retains imports for quoted and unresolved forward references, TYPE_CHECKING, runtime annotation inspection, decorated definitions and complex annotation expressions. This includes dataclasses and Pydantic models: decoration can consume annotations, so modern decorated code may receive no hint even when removal happens to work. Other cases get a conservative review hint, not proof of safe removal. Declared Python 3.14+ targets are handled by TYP001. Repair: Review whether postponement is part of the module's runtime contract, then remove unnecessary boilerplate and verify types and behavior. On Python 3.12/3.13, an annotations future import is appropriate when the chosen public-first order uses forward references; LAY004 preserves eager dependencies when the import is absent. Keep the import if it serves a real purpose; annotate a justified exception if required. Self is only an alternative for methods whose return contract follows the receiver's subclass, such as returning self or constructing cls; a matching class-name annotation alone is insufficient. No Self rewrite is suggested automatically.

typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-r.title: TYP004: An @asynccontextmanager function annotates its return as AsyncIterator[T].
typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-r.description: An @asynccontextmanager function annotates its return as AsyncIterator[T]. The contextlib.asynccontextmanager decorator remains supported. Typeshed deprecates its AsyncIterator overload because the decorator consumes an async generator, including its athrow/aclose methods. Use AsyncGenerator[T, None] to express that contract explicitly; the second argument also works on Python 3.12. This opt-in check provides the same guidance without requiring a type checker. It recognizes async functions and methods with direct AsyncIterator[T] annotations from collections.abc or typing, including quoted annotations, module/import aliases and guarded module-level imports such as TYPE_CHECKING. It conservatively skips names rebound anywhere in the file, wildcard imports, local imports, re-exports, user-defined types, type aliases and wrapped annotations. Ordinary async iterators and functions already annotated as AsyncGenerator remain valid. See https://github.com/python/typeshed/blob/main/stdlib/contextlib.pyi for the deprecated overload. Repair: Replace AsyncIterator[T] with AsyncGenerator[T, None] and import AsyncGenerator from collections.abc. Preserve the yielded type and the decorator, and remove the AsyncIterator import only if unused elsewhere. No automatic rewrite is performed. **TYP004 — typing/deprecated-async-contextmanager-return**

The contextlib.asynccontextmanager decorator remains supported. Typeshed deprecates its AsyncIterator overload because the decorator consumes an async generator, including its athrow/aclose methods. Use AsyncGenerator[T, None] to express that contract explicitly; the second argument also works on Python 3.12. This opt-in check provides the same guidance without requiring a type checker. It recognizes async functions and methods with direct AsyncIterator[T] annotations from collections.abc or typing, including quoted annotations, module/import aliases and guarded module-level imports such as TYPE_CHECKING. async def exclusive() -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    yield
```

**Preferred**

typing/duplicate-literal-type.title: TYP005: Review repeated multi-value Literal types for a shared type alias.
typing/duplicate-literal-type.description: Review repeated multi-value Literal types for a shared type alias. Repeated Literal value sets can drift when a contract changes. This opt-in review groups identical raw value sets within each analyzed root package, including repetitions across modules. It reports one finding per participating file and value set, with related source locations. Direct typing/typing_extensions imports, import aliases, quoted annotations, nested explicit Literals, type aliases and Annotated's first argument are supported. Annotated metadata is never compared or treated as a type. Order and repeated members do not matter; values retain their Python types. Singleton Literals, enum members, named-alias expansion, uncertain imports, test files and separate root packages are excluded. Same-valued types can represent unrelated concepts, so this is a review hint rather than proof that they should share a name. Package rule overrides and suppressions govern findings at each participating file; other analyzed source files still contribute evidence. Repair: Define or reuse a shared plain type alias when the occurrences describe the same concept. Keep Field descriptions and constraints on the Annotated wrappers that need them. Choose an owning module that respects architecture boundaries and avoids import cycles. Review Python-version, runtime annotation and schema behavior before changing aliases; use TypeAlias syntax where the supported Python version requires it. Suppress intentional independent contracts with a reason. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.
typing/duplicate-literal-type.markdownDescription:
**TYP005 — typing/duplicate-literal-type**

Review repeated multi-value Literal types for a shared type alias.

Repeated Literal value sets can drift when a contract changes. This opt-in review groups identical raw value sets within each analyzed root package, including repetitions across modules. It reports one finding per participating file and value set, with related source locations. Direct typing/typing_extensions imports, import aliases, quoted annotations, nested explicit Literals, type aliases and Annotated's first argument are supported. Annotated metadata is never compared or treated as a type. Order and repeated members do not matter; values retain their Python types. Singleton Literals, enum members, named-alias expansion, uncertain imports, test files and separate root packages are excluded. Same-valued types can represent unrelated concepts, so this is a review hint rather than proof that they should share a name. Package rule overrides and suppressions govern findings at each participating file; other analyzed source files still contribute evidence.

**Problem**
```python
from typing import Annotated, Literal
from pydantic import Field

type ClickButton = Annotated[Literal["left", "right"], Field(description="Mouse button")]

def click_message(button: Literal["left", "right"]) -> str:
    return button
```

**Preferred**

from typing import Annotated, Literal
from pydantic import Field

type MouseButton = Literal["left", "right"]
type ClickButton = Annotated[MouseButton, Field(description="Mouse button")]

    return button
```

typing/prefer-deferred-annotations.title: TYP006: An annotation is quoted where deferred evaluation makes quotes unnecessary.
typing/prefer-deferred-annotations.description: An annotation is quoted where deferred evaluation makes quotes unnecessary. Quoted annotations such as list["BrowserWorkspaceTab"] are invisible to rename refactorings, read differently from their neighbors and need a decision at every forward reference. One module-level from __future__ import annotations, or a declared Python 3.14+ minimum, defers every annotation instead. This opt-in style review reports one finding per module that quotes annotations of parameters, returns or annotated assignments: on 3.14+ targets or with the future import, the quotes are redundant; otherwise the module should add the future import. Strings inside Literal and Annotated metadata are values, not annotations, and are ignored, as are quoted names in runtime expressions such as cast() or TypeVar(bound=...). A package contract with future_annotations: forbid keeps quotes on targets before 3.14. Tests are not checked. Repair: Remove the quotes; on targets before Python 3.14 add from __future__ import annotations first. The future import makes every annotation in the module a string at runtime, so verify runtime annotation consumers (dataclasses, Pydantic, FastAPI, dependency injection) and names imported only under TYPE_CHECKING. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {typing/prefer-deferred-annotations: hint}, or select TYP006.

An annotation is quoted where deferred evaluation makes quotes unnecessary.

Quoted annotations such as list["BrowserWorkspaceTab"] are invisible to rename refactorings, read differently from their neighbors and need a decision at every forward reference. One module-level from __future__ import annotations, or a declared Python 3.14+ minimum, defers every annotation instead. This opt-in style review reports one finding per module that quotes annotations of parameters, returns or annotated assignments: on 3.14+ targets or with the future import, the quotes are redundant; otherwise the module should add the future import. Strings inside Literal and Annotated metadata are values, not annotations, and are ignored, as are quoted names in runtime expressions such as cast() or TypeVar(bound=...). A package contract with future_annotations: forbid keeps quotes on targets before 3.14. Tests are not checked.

**Problem**
```python

    @abstractmethod
    async def tabs(self) -> list["BrowserWorkspaceTab"]: ...
```

**Preferred**
```python

class BrowserHandoff(ABC):

```

The future import makes every annotation in the module a string at runtime, so verify runtime annotation consumers (dataclasses, Pydantic, FastAPI, dependency injection) and names imported only under TYPE_CHECKING. typing/anonymous-tuple-type.title: TYP007: A fixed-length tuple type leaves its fields unnamed.
typing/anonymous-tuple-type.description: A fixed-length tuple type leaves its fields unnamed. dict[UUID, tuple[UUID, UUID, BrowserConnection]] does not say which UUID is which; readers decode entry[0] and entry[1] from call sites, and swapping them still type-checks. This opt-in review reports fixed-length tuple types in annotations and type aliases with three or more elements, or with an element type that repeats. Variadic tuple[X, ...], empty tuples, two different element types, quoted annotations, dunder/@override/@overload signatures (dictated elsewhere) and tests are not reported. Repair: Introduce a NamedTuple (keeps unpacking and indexing) or a frozen dataclass that names each field, and use it in place of the tuple. Keep a tuple whose shape an external API dictates with a reasoned suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {typing/anonymous-tuple-type: hint}, or select TYP007.

typing/prefer-inline-type-parameters.title: TYP008: A generic class uses an explicit Generic[...] base on a Python 3.12+ target.
typing/prefer-inline-type-parameters.description: A generic class uses an explicit Generic[...] base on a Python 3.12+ target. PEP 695 puts type parameters on the class declaration and scopes them to the class. This opt-in rule reports parameterized Generic bases resolved through stable, direct module imports from typing or typing_extensions, including aliases. It uses project.python_version or the owning project's requires-python. A minimum below 3.12 or an unknown minimum leaves legacy syntax valid. Generic subclasses without an explicit Generic base, functions and type aliases are outside this check. Ruff UP046 covers similar syntax. Use this rule to apply Smelt's version and package policy. Repair: Declare the parameters on the class, remove the Generic base and keep any other bases. Preserve parameter order, bounds and constraints, and check whether the target supports any parameter defaults. Review inferred variance, shared type variable uses and runtime introspection before migrating. A class that needs to retain explicit variance can use a reasoned Smelt suppression. Enable rules: {typing/prefer-inline-type-parameters: hint}, or select TYP008.

visibility/internal-public-member.title: VIS001: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class.
visibility/internal-public-member.description: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class. An implementation helper should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in package review includes unused definitions and internally used sync/async functions and ordinary instance methods. Imports and module escapes preserve module functions; known test accesses also count as external use, leaving test-only public functions to VIS009. Explicit module __all__ exports and decorated functions are preserved. Methods on decorated, inherited or subclassed classes, special/private methods, properties and class/static methods are excluded. For methods, even unresolved same-named attribute accesses outside the owning class conservatively preserve visibility. External libraries, frameworks, dynamic reflection and unscanned callers cannot be ruled out. This finding asks for review and does not prove a rename is safe. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings preserve their public methods, including aliased re-export chains. Export evidence participates in incremental cache invalidation. Literal lazy-export tables are recognized only with a matching guarded importlib.import_module/getattr forwarder and optional globals cache. The table may supply __all__ through sorted/list/tuple. Arbitrary __getattr__, mutated/escaped tables and stubs alone do not verify runtime exports. Declared composition roots can expose entry points to a runtime and are skipped. Repair: Review the supported interface and callers. For a genuine internal helper, add a leading underscore and update calls and callback references. Resolve existing private-name collisions before renaming. Preserve deliberate public APIs with __all__ for module functions or append `# smelt: ignore[VIS001] -- <specific API reason>` to the reported definition. Keep the concrete reason beside the code; Smelt cannot verify its truth. No automatic rename is performed.

visibility/internal-public-attribute.title: VIS004: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its visibility boundary.
visibility/internal-public-attribute.description: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its visibility boundary. Implementation state should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes, including unused attributes. The default visibility boundary is the owning class. With public_attribute_boundary set to module, production reads and writes in the defining module count as internal access. Any same-named access outside the boundary conservatively preserves visibility, including unresolved receivers, writes, deletions and literal reflection. Test accesses count even when test-quality rules exclude the file; test-only reads remain the responsibility of VIS010, so these rules do not overlap. This also preserves dataclass, attrs, Pydantic, NamedTuple and TypedDict data contracts. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings retain their public attributes, including aliased re-export chains. Inheritance is excluded as a whole rather than attempting to prove which fields a framework or base class owns. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages, external consumers and arbitrary dynamic access are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. This review does not prove that renaming is safe. Repair: Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore and update internal reads and writes, including same-module accesses in module mode. Check name collisions and dynamic consumers. If external callers need to read the value and writes should stay local, consider a read-only property backed by a private field. Preserve deliberate public contracts with a reasoned VIS004 suppression on the declaration or a package rule override. Suggested names avoid observed collisions. Smelt leaves renaming to the caller. Enable the rule in rules, select VIS004, or set public_attribute_boundary under style or in a style override.

visibility/foreign-private-access.title: VIS005: Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module.
visibility/foreign-private-access.description: Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module. A leading underscore marks a name as private to its owner. Reaching into a collaborator's private helpers, fields or methods couples the caller to implementation details. This opt-in review reports two kinds of access. symbol: relative and absolute from-imports and module-qualified reads of a module-level private name, through lexical import aliases, when it statically resolves to a definition in another analyzed production module, including sibling modules of the same package. Public aliases remain public, and a package initializer may re-export its own submodule's private symbol under a public alias. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking. attribute: reads, writes, calls, updates and deletes of a private member, such as self.log._images, whose receiver and defining project class are statically known and live in another module, or another package under style.private_attribute_boundary: package. Direct accesses on the method receiver to its own or inherited members are allowed. Receiver evidence comes from parameter/variable annotations, direct constructor assignments, stable local aliases, class/instance fields, property return annotations and bounded single inheritance; import aliases, relative imports and static facade re-exports resolve to the defining class. Unlike Ruff SLF001, unresolved receivers are not reported. Dunders, third-party and unknown names, private module names, reflection, same-module access, unknown factories, inherited lookup across multiple/unknown bases, arbitrary class decorators, local imports in attribute evidence, comprehension/lambda receiver bodies, closure/global-variable flow, rebound or shadowed bindings and wildcard imports are skipped. Tests are covered by tests/private-access (TST002). No control-flow narrowing, runtime dispatch or analyzed code execution is used. Preserve evaluation order, exceptions and side effects. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/foreign-private-access: warning}, select VIS005, or set private_attribute_boundary under style or in a style override. visibility/foreign-private-access.markdownDescription:
**VIS005 — visibility/foreign-private-access**

Production code uses a private symbol or private attribute owned by another project module.

A leading underscore marks a name as private to its owner. Reaching into a collaborator's private helpers, fields or methods couples the caller to implementation details. This opt-in review reports two kinds of access. symbol: relative and absolute from-imports and module-qualified reads of a module-level private name, through lexical import aliases, when it statically resolves to a definition in another analyzed production module, including sibling modules of the same package. Public aliases remain public, and a package initializer may re-export its own submodule's private symbol under a public alias. TYPE_CHECKING follows architecture.import_graph.type_checking. attribute: reads, writes, calls, updates and deletes of a private member, such as self.log._images, whose receiver and defining project class are statically known and live in another module, or another package under style.private_attribute_boundary: package. Direct accesses on the method receiver to its own or inherited members are allowed. Receiver evidence comes from parameter/variable annotations, direct constructor assignments, stable local aliases, class/instance fields, property return annotations and bounded single inheritance; import aliases, relative imports and static facade re-exports resolve to the defining class. Unlike Ruff SLF001, unresolved receivers are not reported. Dunders, third-party and unknown names, private module names, reflection, same-module access, unknown factories, inherited lookup across multiple/unknown bases, arbitrary class decorators, local imports in attribute evidence, comprehension/lambda receiver bodies, closure/global-variable flow, rebound or shadowed bindings and wildcard imports are skipped. Tests are covered by tests/private-access (TST002). No control-flow narrowing, runtime dispatch or analyzed code execution is used.

**Problem**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.session import SessionLog
from .service import _normalize
def persist(log: SessionLog):
    return _normalize(log._images.retain())
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.session import SessionLog
from .service import normalize
def persist(log: SessionLog):
    return normalize(log.retain_images())
```

For attributes, expose a meaningful operation on the owning class or pass a deliberate public dependency; do not merely rename or wrap internal state to silence the report. Preserve evaluation order, exceptions and side effects. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable rules: {visibility/foreign-private-access: warning}, select VIS005, or set private_attribute_boundary under style or in a style override. The boundary defaults to module; package permits attribute cooperation between modules of the same immediate Python package and does not relax private symbols. Reasoned suppressions on the imported name, read or attribute are supported.
